title: Expose authoritative light rendering state for display clients
body:
## Ownership

The fresh Linux installation's existing worker owns light writes and the timeline it sends. This issue exposes a read-only snapshot of that worker output. The wall map's live renderer and physical parity belong to [#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17); this issue does not change current wall-map animation. Legacy Windows installations keep their existing path; adding Windows-specific behavior is outside scope.

Reuse relevant fields from [agent-device-hub#4](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/4) where useful. The shared overview and basic controls do not wait for this work.

## Desired outcome

Provide display clients with enough last-sent rendering data to reproduce bridge-controlled output without inferring it from task status or scheduling effects themselves.

## Scope

Add a read-only `GET /api/rendering` route to the existing loopback wall-map server for the current Linux-owned Lines worker. Read directly from private state without refreshing metadata, acquiring device geometry, contacting the controller, or starting a worker. Include physical zone identity, encoded colors and frame durations, loop/effect phase, effective brightness and a compact outcome: pending, last successfully sent, failed/partial, or externally controlled/unknown.

Retain only the latest output receipt needed to describe the current worker output; do not add output history, subscriptions, replay queues, a new listener/authentication system, or a second writer. Preserve existing task/effect epochs and the current palette, one outward pulse with its two-second cycle, completion comet defaults, split project/status halves, and Work/Quiet/Free behavior. Future palettes and effects remain with #18-#20.

A successful HTTP command means the device accepted the command; it does not prove what the lights visibly produced. Scenes or streams whose frames are unavailable remain externally controlled/unknown. A simulated on-screen preview is not live worker output.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A rendering read provides the worker's last successfully accepted encoded frames, physical zone identity, frame durations, looping/phase and brightness needed by a display client to reproduce bridge-controlled output.
- AC2: The response distinguishes pending work, last successful output, failed or partially accepted updates, and external/unknown output. It does not describe command acceptance as optical confirmation.
- AC3: Reads do not refresh task metadata, advance effects, reserve sources, clear unread state, change assignments/preferences, acquire device geometry, contact the controller, start a worker, or write lights. Reads and reconnects do not replay expired effects.
- AC4: The latest output receipt and timing remain available after worker or map-server restart without resetting task, scene or project preferences. Existing installations acquire receipt storage without destructive migration.
- AC5: The endpoint reads through the existing loopback server and retains its Host and no-store protections. It contains no Nanoleaf credentials. Current wall-map rendering remains unchanged; #17 consumes this data.

## Verification

Use the fake controller, isolated database and fake clock to compare representative worker payloads for a two-second pulse and completion comet. Check pending and failed/partial outcomes, repeated reads, restart recovery, and that the GET-only rendering endpoint rejects writes without changing the last-sent worker receipt. The renderer-specific check that an on-screen-only preview stays separate from live worker output belongs to #17.

For implementation, run `python3 scripts/check.py`. The wall map itself is unchanged, so browser rendering checks belong with #17. Physical comparison and installation remain separate, explicitly authorized work under #17/#55.

## Dependencies

None. The shared envelope in agent-device-hub#4 is available for alignment; it does not block this work. The ambient-view decision and Lively prototype do not gate it.

## Follow-up work

- [#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17) - Render bridge-controlled lights live and verify physical parity.
- [#18](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/18) - Configure project and status colors.
- [#19](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/19) - Choose and preview completion celebrations.
- [#20](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/20) - Customize animation for each status.
- [#16](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/16) - Build the deferred ambient view.
- [#21](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/21) - Investigate mirroring externally controlled Nanoleaf scenes.

title: Build the ambient view
body:
## Desired outcome

If selected after the Lively prototype, provide a spacious ambient wall visualization that communicates task status and offers details on demand.

## Scope

Deferred ambient work. Reuse the Lively integration and the live renderer from #17, supporting fullscreen browser use. Consume the effective palettes from #18, celebration choices from #19, and per-status animations from #20 through #15's shared output contract. Add an uncluttered wall presentation, on-demand inspection, and reduced-motion support. Settle idle and Work/Quiet/Free presentation and the performance budget using the prototype findings before implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: An approved design defines idle, Work, Quiet, and Free presentation, inspection, and reduced-motion behavior. Do not imply that the display mirrors arbitrary Nanoleaf scenes unless a separate capability supports that claim.
- AC2: Physical Line numbering, project/task associations, status meaning, and waiting-task visibility remain consistent with the normal map.
- AC3: Reuse #17's renderer and #15's output/timing contract with the user's effective palettes, celebration choices, and status-animation settings. Reconnection and resume do not replay expired effects. Blocked and question alerts retain their semantic priority and remain recognizable regardless of selected hues. Any reduced-motion presentation is explicit rather than being presented as an exact animated live mirror.
- AC4: Details are available on demand without exposing assignment, palette, animation, celebration, mode, Locate, or physical-preview controls. Configuration remains in the regular app. Selection does not change bridge state or mark tasks read.
- AC5: The view works in the verified Lively configuration and a fullscreen browser at the tested display size. Reduced-motion behavior and text/indicator contrast are reviewed with the user.
- AC6: Resource use is measured against #14's baseline and meets a budget agreed before implementation. Account for visible, covered/paused, and resumed behavior.
- AC7: The user approves the current UI candidate before merge. Record source, installed display, and any physical-light evidence separately.

## Verification approach

Use deterministic timing and browser scenarios for status semantics, overlapping animation, expired effects, recovery, inspection, and reduced motion. Compare actual Windows resource measurements and readability with the prototype. Run the canonical Python, browser, and applicable workflow checks.

Deliver through an isolated worktree and reviewed PR. Use an issue-linked OpenSpec change for changed behavior, focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, every configured CI job, and main CI readback. UI changes require explicit human approval of the current candidate before merge. Keep revision-specific evidence in the PR.

## Dependencies

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/14 - Run and evaluate the installed Lively prototype
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/15 - Expose authoritative light rendering state for display clients
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17 - Show bridge-controlled lights live in the app
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/18 - Configure project and status colors consistently
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/19 - Choose and preview completion celebrations
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/20 - Customize animation for each status

Deferred and blocked until the source prerequisites and #14 evaluation are complete and the user explicitly chooses the ambient direction. Resolve presentation and performance decisions before this issue becomes ready. The independent foundation/customization work does not inherit this ambient decision gate.

## Delivery target

Source-only future work. Installed verification requires separate authorization. A custom desktop widget, new wallpaper engine, and arbitrary Nanoleaf scene mirroring are outside this issue.

## Related investigation

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/21 - Investigate mirroring externally controlled Nanoleaf scenes

External-scene mirroring is a separate capability. Unsupported output remains identified honestly; this issue does not introduce a controller observer or emulate scene phase without evidence.

## Related work: wall assembly

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/38 - Animate wall assembly from a central orb

Reuse the wall-assembly presentation for supported view-entry transitions. Keep playback preferences in the regular app. Reconnection and Lively pause/resume do not trigger assembly. Ambient adoption remains subject to this issue’s existing evaluation, design, and approval gates.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** The owner's ambient-direction choice and a re-scope of acceptance criteria 5 and 6 around the Linux runtime, as the 2026-09-24 comment asks.

**Reassess when:** The owner chooses the ambient direction.

title: Show bridge-controlled lights live in the app
body:
## Shared-hub ownership
Keep the reusable Nanoleaf visual renderer here. Future hub previews may consume this timeline after parity verification; [agent-device-hub#6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6)'s overview does not depend on it. Do not add a device writer or status interpreter.

## Desired outcome

Make the regular app's wall visualization track bridge-controlled physical lights in real time, including animation rather than only one-second status-color updates.

## Scope

Consume #15's rendering contract in a reusable visual renderer for the current map. Match task pulses and waves, per-project halves, completion effects, Locate, and physical previews. Make the renderer reusable by the inspection-only wallpaper and future ambient view without requiring either deliverable to finish first.

Keep on-screen effect demonstrations visibly separate from the live wall visualization. External Nanoleaf scenes are a separate investigation.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: For bridge-controlled output, the correct physical zones show the same encoded colors, relative brightness, frame transitions, looping, and timing as the worker output. Project/status halves and physical Line numbering remain correct after rotation and flips.
- AC2: Verify a maximum visual phase difference of 250 ms in the agreed visible-app acceptance scenarios on the user's PC. Record actual measurements and the measurement method. This measures UI-versus-wall alignment, not the separate delay before a task-status event reaches the worker. A failure to meet the target remains an acceptance gap unless the user explicitly revises it.
- AC3: Rendering follows successfully sent output and exposes pending, failed/uncertain, stale, and externally controlled states. Do not present requested-but-unsent settings or arbitrary scene guesses as current physical output.
- AC4: Pause/resume, browser backgrounding, reconnect, server restart, and task interruption recover to current output without replaying expired waves or celebrations.
- AC5: Selecting Lines/tasks and observing the live view do not mutate task state, mark tasks read, start animations, or send light writes. Existing editing actions remain explicit in the regular map; the wallpaper remains inspection-only.
- AC6: An on-screen preview is labeled and separate from live output. A physical preview appears in the live view while the worker plays it, and normal current output returns afterward.
- AC7: Physical comparison covers Work and Quiet, overlapping blocked/question alerts, split halves, an existing completion comet, and Locate. Extend frame-parity and device scenarios when the linked new palettes and effects become available. Free and idle external scenes display their known control state without claiming unverified per-zone mirroring.
- AC8: Preserve keyboard focus and selection during updates, and record CPU/GPU/memory behavior while visible and paused. No second animation scheduler or light writer is introduced.

## Verification approach

Use deterministic frame/timing browser scenarios against #15, including failed/partial sends and restart/no-replay cases. Compare the visible UI with physical output using synchronized recording or another reproducible observation method with sufficient timing resolution. Include representative animation transitions and report observed maximum skew. Matching software frames alone does not establish physical synchronization.

Run python3 scripts/check.py after Python changes, npm run test:browser after map/API changes, and npm run check:workflow plus npm run test:workflow after npm ci for OpenSpec/workflow changes. Validate PowerShell changes in Windows PowerShell.

Deliver source changes through an isolated worktree and reviewed PR, using an issue-linked OpenSpec change for changed behavior. Use focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, all configured CI jobs, and main CI readback. UI changes require explicit human approval of the current candidate before merge. Keep revision-specific evidence in the PR.

## Dependencies

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/15 - Expose authoritative light rendering state for display clients

Blocked until #15 provides the rendering contract. Lively prototype evaluation is not a prerequisite. Coordinate future renderer use with #12 and #16 while preserving their scopes.

## Delivery target

Source delivery followed by explicitly authorized installed Windows/device verification. Keep this issue open until the required physical synchronization evidence is complete. Use bridge/install-modes.ps1 for an authorized upgrade, preserve live state, and identify the installation owner before a trial.

## Follow-up work

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/18 - Configure project and status colors consistently
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/19 - Choose and preview completion celebrations

## Related work

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/21 - Investigate mirroring externally controlled Nanoleaf scenes

The inspection-only wallpaper may reuse this renderer after both are available; it gains no configuration or physical-preview controls.

title: Keep the live wall view consistent with the configured palette
body:
> Scope narrowed on 2026-09-24. [#139](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/139) now owns the configurable base and status palette: the color choices, defaults, persistence, reset, validation, status-based priority, physical output, Project halves and the current map's artwork and legend. This issue keeps only the part that depends on the live renderer from #17. The original scope is in this issue's edit history.

## Shared-hub ownership

Use shared semantic identifiers from [agent-device-hub#2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/2) with an explicit mapping for current working/question/blocked/unread behavior. Palettes and brightness stay device presentation preferences. Priority cannot derive from RGB; clients consume effective colors.

## Desired outcome

Once #17 draws the wall from the worker's sent frames, every color the regular app shows agrees with the palette the worker is using, including while a palette change is still being applied.

## Scope

After #17, the map has two color sources: the worker's sent frames from #15 and the effective palette from #139, which colors the legend and task status markers. Make them agree, and show a palette change as pending until the worker has sent frames with it. Palette editing, storage, defaults and physical output stay with #139. On-screen previews belong to #19 and #20, which take their colors from #139. Exposing the palette to the CLI, controller API, MCP or integration settings API stays deferred under #139's revisit trigger.

If #17's delivery already meets these criteria, close this issue with that evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: With a custom palette, the live view's Line colors match the worker's sent frames, and the legend and task status markers use the same effective palette.
- AC2: After a palette change, the live view keeps the previously sent colors and marks the change pending until the worker sends frames with the new palette. A failed send shows as failed, not as the requested colors.
- AC3: The browser keeps no fixed status-color table. Wherever #17's renderer draws a status color that does not come from a frame, it reads the effective palette from #139.
- AC4: Viewing the live wall and changing the palette do not restart status epochs, replay waves or completions, change task/Line assignments or mark tasks read. Work, Quiet and Free behavior and saved scenes are unchanged.

## Verification approach

Browser tests with a custom palette cover a pending palette change, a failed send, the legend and task status markers. Compare live-view colors with frame colors from the fake worker. Record software evidence separately from physical observations.

Run `python3 scripts/check.py` after Python changes, `npm run test:browser` after map/API changes, and `npm run check:workflow` plus `npm run test:workflow` after `npm ci` for OpenSpec/workflow changes.

Deliver source changes through an isolated worktree and reviewed PR, using an issue-linked OpenSpec change for changed behavior. Use focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, all configured CI jobs, and main CI readback. UI changes require explicit human approval of the current candidate before merge. Keep revision-specific evidence in the PR.

## Dependencies

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17 - Show bridge-controlled lights live in the app
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/139 - Customize Work-mode light colors so unread tasks stand out from the base

Blocked until #17 and #139 are delivered. #15 and agent-device-hub#2 are complete.

## Delivery target

Source-only. A physical comparison needs a separately authorized check on the Linux installation.

## Related work

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/20 - Customize animation for each status

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against `main` at `7a030ac`, after the 2026-09-24 narrowing.

- **Complexity: low.** A few browser color paths and their tests, once #17's renderer exists.
- **Uncertainty: high.** The live renderer this story adjusts is not built yet, so whether any code is needed is unknown until #17 lands.

title: Choose and preview completion celebrations
body:
## Desired outcome

Let the user select different completion celebrations, choose project overrides, and preview effects on screen or explicitly on the physical wall.

## Scope

Add one default celebration with optional per-project overrides. The initial preset set is Comet, outward Ripple, Sparkle, and None. Keep the existing Comet as the upgrade default. Reuse the live renderer and configurable colors rather than implementing independent browser-only effects.

Provide an on-screen preview by default and a separate explicit Preview on lights action in the regular app. This does not add preview controls to the inspection-only wallpaper.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Every project uses its override when present and otherwise inherits the default. The app makes inheritance clear and can remove an override. Choices survive restarts and upgrades.
- AC2: Comet preserves its current default behavior. Ripple travels outward from the task's assigned Line; Sparkle provides a distinct finite effect. Presets have stable identifiers, documented durations, and reproducible frames. Any randomness is fixed per playback so preview and live output can agree.
- AC3: None disables only the celebration. It does not remove the unread indicator, mark a task read, or release an assignment that unread tracking still requires.
- AC4: Existing completion eligibility, queue ordering, unread handling, interruption, and active-source reservations are retained for every preset. Resolve the chosen preset/configuration for each queued completion so subsequent edits cannot restart or rewrite an in-flight effect. Source reservations last until that effect's actual end.
- AC5: Browsing or starting an on-screen preview changes no physical lights, live task records, assignments, unread state, or completion queue. Label the preview and keep it separate from the live wall view.
- AC6: Preview on lights is an explicit protected request handled by the single Windows worker. It is cancellable, respects blocked/question alert priority, and cannot consume or discard real queued completions. Define serialization with active celebrations and Locate; do not interrupt a reserved source or silently drop a request.
- AC7: Physical previews operate in Work. Quiet remains steady and Free leaves physical control with Nanoleaf; the UI explains when physical preview is unavailable without changing modes automatically. On-screen demonstrations remain available without altering the selected mode.
- AC8: Ending, cancelling, timing out, or failing a physical preview restores the current task display or appropriate current scene behavior, not a stale snapshot taken before preview. Mode changes and worker restart preserve task state and cannot leave a looping preview or replay it.
- AC9: The live view tracks the actual physical preview through #15. All presets preserve semantic alert priority and the selected project/status animation-coverage behavior.
- AC10: Selection, reset, and preview controls are accessible in the regular UI. Existing hooks and the definition of a completion event remain unchanged.

## Verification approach

Use fake-clock/device tests for all preset durations, inheritance, None, queue order, simultaneous completions, source reservations, active/queued settings edits, interruption, cancellation, mode changes, failed sends, and worker restart. Browser tests verify selection, inheritance, preview labeling, no live mutations from on-screen preview, and explicit physical-preview requests. Physical preview/restore behavior needs an authorized Windows/device trial and recorded observations.

Run python3 scripts/check.py after Python changes, npm run test:browser after map/API changes, and npm run check:workflow plus npm run test:workflow after npm ci for OpenSpec/workflow changes. Validate PowerShell changes in Windows PowerShell.

Deliver source changes through an isolated worktree and reviewed PR, using an issue-linked OpenSpec change for changed behavior. Use focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, all configured CI jobs, and main CI readback. UI changes require explicit human approval of the current candidate before merge. Keep revision-specific evidence in the PR.

## Dependencies

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/15 - Expose authoritative light rendering state for display clients
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17 - Show bridge-controlled lights live in the app
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/18 - Configure project and status colors consistently

Blocked until shared rendering, the live view, and consistent palettes are available. Use issue-linked OpenSpec design to settle preset timing and preview scheduling before implementation. A custom animation editor and random rotation among presets are outside this issue.

## Delivery target

Source-only feature delivery. Record source checks separately from installed preview and physical restoration evidence; the latter require explicit trial/upgrade authorization and an installation owner.

## Follow-up work

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/16 - Build the ambient view (deferred)

title: Customize animation for each status
body:
## Desired outcome

Let working, question, blocked, and unread statuses use independently chosen animation presets, speed, and intensity while retaining their meaning and precedence.

## Scope

Provide per-status presets and controls in the regular app, with reset to the current defaults. The initial presets are the existing Pulse, gentle Breathing, and Steady illumination. Keep the initial outward indication and ongoing local status animation distinct. This is preset-based customization, not a full animation editor.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Each status independently selects a preset, cycle duration/speed, and intensity within documented valid ranges. Explain controls in user terms and make inapplicable controls unavailable for Steady.
- AC2: Upgrade defaults reproduce the current pulse, two-second cycle, intensity envelope, and single outward indication. Reset affects only the selected animation settings, preserving colors, projects, task records, modes, and scenes.
- AC3: Define and validate control ranges against controller frame timing and visibility needs before implementation. Intensity must not silently change the mode's overall brightness or erase the ongoing status indicator.
- AC4: Blocked/question precedence remains status-based for all presets and custom palettes. Existing split halves and animation coverage remain consistent with saved project preferences.
- AC5: Animation changes apply at a documented boundary without restarting a task/status epoch, repeating its initial outward indication, or replaying a completion. Define phase behavior when speed or preset changes during activity and test it.
- AC6: Quiet remains steady regardless of a Work animation preset. Free continues to leave physical lighting to Nanoleaf. Changes preserve the mode and scene selections.
- AC7: Persist preferences across restart and upgrade; invalid or unknown values fail safely to documented behavior without resetting unrelated preferences.
- AC8: Physical output and the live map use the same effective settings and #15 timing contract. Preview demonstrations, if shown, use the shared renderer and remain distinct from current physical output.
- AC9: Controls remain in the regular app. The inspection-only wallpaper and future ambient view consume configured output without exposing these mutations.

## Verification approach

Use fake-clock frame tests for each preset, min/max values, independent statuses, active speed/preset edits, no-replay behavior, priority overlap, modes, and persistence/migration. Add browser checks for controls, resets, invalid values, and map/output agreement. Record physical visual acceptance separately from automated tests.

Run python3 scripts/check.py after Python changes, npm run test:browser after map/API changes, and npm run check:workflow plus npm run test:workflow after npm ci for OpenSpec/workflow changes. Validate PowerShell changes in Windows PowerShell.

Deliver source changes through an isolated worktree and reviewed PR, using an issue-linked OpenSpec change for changed behavior. Use focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, all configured CI jobs, and main CI readback. UI changes require explicit human approval of the current candidate before merge. Keep revision-specific evidence in the PR.

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17 - Show bridge-controlled lights live in the app
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/18 - Configure project and status colors consistently

title: Check feasibility of mirroring externally controlled Nanoleaf scenes
body:
## Desired outcome

Decide whether externally controlled Nanoleaf output can be observed well enough to justify a later live mirror. If it cannot, the app should show an honest externally controlled/unknown state.

## Scope

Review authoritative API documentation first. Consider three output groups: solid colors and static saved scenes; animated or randomized saved scenes; and externally driven output such as music and Screen Mirror. Distinguish current per-zone output and animation phase from a scene name, palette, effect definition, or global setting. This investigation does not block the bridge-controlled live view in #17.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Identify documented read-only observation methods for each output group. State whether they expose current per-zone colors and brightness, animation phase, only metadata, or nothing relevant. Cite the evidence and its limits. A scene definition or palette alone is not proof of current physical output.
- AC2: Summarize each group as observable, partly observable, or unknown, and recommend whether live mirroring is worth pursuing. If documentation shows no plausible way to observe current per-zone output and phase for a group, stop there and recommend an externally controlled/unknown UI state for it. An undocumented method is not proof that observation is impossible.
- AC3: If a plausible read-only method exists, define one small follow-up device trial to verify it. Measure timing and controller impact only in that later trial if actual frame data is available; #17's 250 ms target applies to bridge-controlled output and is not an acceptance target for this documentation review.
- AC4: Preserve Free mode's no-polling-after-handoff behavior. This issue adds no polling, light control, stream, competing writer, scene emulation, or credentials in the browser. Any device trial or change to Free-mode observation needs its own authorized scope and an identified device owner.

## Verification approach

Start with the [official Nanoleaf API documentation](https://nanoleaf.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/nlapid/pages/2789310530/Nanoleaf+Light+Panels+Open+API+Documentation) and its [documentation index](https://support.nanoleaf.me/hc/en-us/articles/46020382680468-API-Nanoleaf-OpenAPI-Documentation-Forum-Guidelines). Record the relevant methods and what their responses actually establish. Do not treat an effect listing, a successful HTTP response, or a documented write stream as current-frame telemetry.

## Dependencies

None. Coordinate terminology with #15's rendering/freshness model and #17's externally controlled state. No Lively or ambient work is required.

## Delivery target

A brief evidence table and a recommendation for each output group. Stop at findings and, only where warranted, one bounded follow-up trial proposal. No source changes, installation, controller exercises, or physical-light acceptance are part of this issue.

## Related work

- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/15 - Expose authoritative light rendering state for display clients
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17 - Show bridge-controlled lights live in the app
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/16 - Build the ambient view (deferred)

title: Keep map number tags clear of neighbouring Lines in rotated compact layouts
body:
## Desired outcome

Line numbers fit the Prism crystal style and remain easy to identify and select without overlapping neighbouring Lines. Show neutral luminous numerals for selected, highlighted, hovered, and keyboard-focused Lines, with an optional show-all control.

## Scope

Refine this existing number-clearance issue as part of the approved Prism work. Keep its unresolved compact-layout regression and stable-identity requirements. Do not create a duplicate numbering issue.

Original reproduction from the #22 review in PR #24: at 90 or 270 degrees in 800×844 and 390×844 layouts, tags 6, 7, 10, and 11 sit within or close to a neighbouring Line's track. The earlier tags cleared their own selection ring but used the side away from the wall center. Keep neighbour clearance as the placement goal when replacing pill tags with luminous numerals. Use the final crystal body and selection bounds rather than assuming the old 10-unit track or 12-unit selected half-width is still correct.

The default visibility follows selected/highlighted/hovered/focused Lines. Multiple selected Lines can show their numbers at once. Show-all is a browser-local display preference, off by default; it never changes physical lights or bridge allocation. Preserve the inspector, task/project associations, pending selection state, multi-selection modifiers, and explicit Locate action. Exclude physical renumbering, a general layout editor, tray work, and service migration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: At 1440, 800, and 390 px, every supported map rotation and flip has no numeral/label bounds intersecting a neighbouring Line's final crystal track or active selection bounds. Labels remain inside the canvas. Cover the original compact-layout regression, the show-all state, and multiple simultaneously selected/highlighted labels. Preserve the existing all-rotations overlap guard and adapt it to the final material geometry.
- [x] AC2: Preserve the existing 360 raw number-click cases across three widths and eight orientations, using show-all for that complete identity check. Numerals retain a legible text height of at least 11 px and no horizontal overflow. Glow cannot replace the readable numeral core or obscure nearby labels.
- [x] AC3: Physical numbering, stable Line IDs, click targets, and task/project/inspector associations remain unchanged across rotation, flips, mode changes, polling, and geometry refresh. Ctrl/Cmd/Shift multi-selection keeps the app's existing behavior. Connectors and decorative light layers do not intercept number or Line selection.
- [x] AC4: Default mode reveals a Line's numeral whenever it is selected, highlighted, hovered, or keyboard-focused. Removing one reason does not hide the numeral while another remains. Idle unselected/unhighlighted/unhovered/unfocused Lines hide their numbers; show-all reveals every number. Touch selection can reveal and retain a number without requiring hover.
- [x] AC5: Numerals use a neutral luminous treatment with a crisp readable core and restrained spill, visually consistent with Prism without adopting a task/status color. They remain readable in Work, Quiet, Free, and reduced motion. Keyboard focus and selected/pending state remain distinguishable. Accessible names retain stable Line numbers even when decorative numerals are hidden.
- [x] AC6: Hover, focus, selection, and show-all issue no light, assignment, unread, or Locate request. An interaction during assembly settles the structure and performs the intended action; it does not discard the selection or reveal stale labels. The existing explicit Locate control remains the only path for that device action.

## Verification approach

All checks below are planned, not executed by this issue update.

| Criteria | Planned evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC1, AC2 | Extend `tests/foundation_checks.cjs` clearance checks with final label/body bounds and all supported rotations/flips. Retain the 360 click checks with show-all. Capture original failing compact poses and final screenshots; assert minimum text size, viewport containment, and no horizontal overflow. |
| AC3, AC4 | Browser journeys for modifier multi-selection, external highlighting, hover exit while selected, focus/blur, touch selection, show-all persistence, and surviving IDs after geometry refresh. Assert stable labels and cross-view associations. |
| AC5 | Keyboard and accessible-name assertions, mode/reduced-motion matrix, and human desktop/mobile review at final glow settings. Automated bounds do not establish visual legibility on their own. |
| AC6 | Request spies and synthetic-state snapshots during selection/show-all and assembly interruption; assert no new device or state mutation. Retain explicit Locate tests separately. |

Run `npm run test:browser`. Run `python3 scripts/check.py` if Python changes become necessary. After `npm ci` and the issue-linked OpenSpec changes, run `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow`. Record actual commands and candidate revision during delivery, not as planning results.

## Dependencies and scope references

- Blocked by https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/53 for final crystal dimensions, interaction integration, and material appearance. Placement investigation can run independently; final acceptance uses the integrated Prism renderer.
- Original prerequisite [#22](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/22) is satisfied by [PR #24](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/24).
- Preserve [wall-line-identification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/openspec/specs/wall-line-identification/spec.md) and the interaction/phase contracts of [wall-assembly-animation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/openspec/specs/wall-assembly-animation/spec.md). Add explicit deltas for luminous styling and conditional visibility while retaining numbering and clearance guarantees.

## Assessment

Planning update, 2026-09-09, current main `ea3b95661352f927aceaf92b62d74660978c201f`, original #26 reproduction and the accepted Prism selection preference.

- Complexity: medium. Collision-aware placement, several visibility reasons, multi-selection, and responsive transforms must stay consistent.
- Uncertainty: medium. The bounded investigation compares neighbour clearance in the known failing poses after final crystal bounds are available. Choose the smallest placement change that satisfies the full visibility/rotation matrix without reducing the 11 px floor.
- Impact: medium. Regressions can misidentify a Line or make selection inaccessible; interactions must remain local and retain identity.
- Readiness: blocked by the Prism integration. Product choices are settled. Reassess if final dimensions, interaction contracts, or supported orientations change.

## Delivery target and handoff

Source-only. This planning update preserves the issue's existing open state, ownership, and unrelated metadata; it starts no implementation or device operation.

Future delivery follows the current SDLC with an owned worktree, this issue's exact OpenSpec change, current checks/CI, independent Standards and Specification reviews, and human approval of the integrated UI candidate before merge. Include accessibility and visual-clearance review. The coordinator records accepted screenshots and hands over no installation or physical-light claim.

The authorized follow-up must reflect this changed issue scope and record it in `docs/work-guide/updates.md` through a linked Hub companion PR under the [guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md). This issue update does not publish repository PRs or the public guide.

title: Consume shared agent sessions while preserving Nanoleaf behavior
body:
## Outcome
Render qualified Codex and Claude sessions from the shared state owner without duplicating provider interpretation.

## Scope
Add shared input to the existing Python worker using versioned snapshots/events. Opt-in means an explicit, persisted choice of legacy or shared task input for the selected installation; installing or upgrading the software does not switch sources. After verified cutover, the shared state owner becomes the authoritative source of agent/session status for that installation and remains selected across restarts. Legacy Codex ingestion remains available for explicit rollback. Initial shared hosting is the Pixoo backend under [divoom-app-upgrade#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31), with standalone hosting later.

Source selection is independent of Work/Quiet/Free. Shared input supplies task status; the existing Python worker remains the sole light writer and continues to enforce the selected device mode. This issue owns consumer configuration, source selection and recovery behavior. [Hub #8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8) owns reversible producer/hook setup and cutover tooling; [#30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/30) owns installed, real-client and physical acceptance. Define the supported configuration/command interface in the issue-linked design and expose its sanitized state to the integration-settings API; no existing switch is implied.

Use the fresh Linux runtime delivered by [#54](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/54) as the primary baseline, following [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-linux-runtime-ownership.md). Keep runtime SQLite private to the selected installation and operating system. Legacy Windows installations retain their own Windows runtime and forwarding path. Shared-input cutover and rollback remain separate from the fresh Linux installation and do not import Windows runtime state into Linux.

The [hub architecture](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#ownership) keeps provider/session interpretation in the shared core and device presentation in Nanoleaf. title: Get shared Codex monitoring working on the existing Linux Nanoleaf installation
body:
## Outcome

Get shared Codex monitoring working on the user's existing Linux/WSL Nanoleaf installation, then verify it with real tasks and visible light behavior. This is a personal-project update: temporary breakage and repair are acceptable.

## Scope

Perform a one-off update of the installed program and dependencies, configure shared monitoring using [Hub #8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8), restart the relevant processes, and fix problems found during real use. Use the shared consumer delivered by [#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29).

The selected installation is the user's existing Linux/WSL runtime at `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf`, owned by the user. Start with Codex Desktop tasks executing in WSL and Codex CLI in WSL. Use the existing Nanoleaf interface; the shared frontend is not required for this issue.

No reusable Linux installer or upgrade framework is required. A documented one-off update is sufficient. Keep credentials private, keep runtime SQLite on Linux, avoid duplicate task ingestion, and use one designated Python light-writing worker. Preserve unrelated applications, hooks and Codex data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Record the source revision used, installed runtime location and actual Codex Desktop/CLI versions. Update the existing Linux program files and required dependencies, configure shared monitoring, and restart the relevant owned processes. Record the commands that actually worked.
- [x] Confirm shared input is selected and remains selected after an ordinary restart. Use the existing source-selection commands and their built-in checks; no new cutover mechanism or formal migration qualification is required. Work/Quiet/Free remains a separate device-mode choice.
- [x] Run a real Codex Desktop task executing in WSL and a real Codex CLI task in WSL. Confirm their activity reaches the shared owner and Nanoleaf without duplicate ingestion. Record any missing client behavior honestly; do not substitute simulated events for these real-client checks.
- [x] With the device target identified and permission for the light test, observe task activity and completion on the actual lights. Check the existing Nanoleaf interface and basic Work/Quiet/Free behavior. Keep command/transport results separate from the user's visible-light observations.
- [x] Fix problems that prevent this basic workflow from working. Finish with one designated Linux worker, a working installation, and the user's chosen final mode. Record remaining limitations and a short restart/troubleshooting note.

## Not required for completion

- A separate Linux upgrade deliverable, reusable updater, automated backup/rollback tooling, or interrupted-upgrade recovery.
- A guaranteed safe cutover, a comprehensive rollback trial, or restoring an earlier installation as an acceptance gate. Existing switch-back commands may remain available without additional qualification.
- Guaranteed preservation of old task history, assignments, preferences, scene state or animation timing through this one-off update. Repair and reconfiguration are acceptable; this does not authorize deleting unrelated user data.
- Repeated migration rehearsals, exhaustive outage/reconnect/removal/revocation scenarios, concurrency stress tests, a soak period, or a full provider qualification matrix.
- Windows-owned installation/forwarding qualification or Claude qualification. These are deferred beyond this issue, not reported as passing.
- Shared-frontend acceptance from [Hub #6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6), integrated performance qualification from [Hub #30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30), or exact map/light parity from [#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17). These do not block this smaller finish line.

## Dependencies and related work

Required source inputs:
- [Nanoleaf #29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29): shared consumer.
- [Hub #8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8): shared-monitoring setup tooling.

[#54](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/54) supplies the Linux runtime. [#55](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/55) retains its separately owned baseline acceptance; this issue does not deliver or close it. [#49](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/49) supplies the existing settings API, but exhaustive settings/assignment qualification is outside this issue. Broader shared integration remains tracked by [Hub #32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32).

## Verification and delivery

Reuse applicable source test evidence and run focused checks for any fixes. Prioritize the actual installed Codex-to-lights path over additional simulated migration coverage. Repository source changes still follow the applicable PR, review and test workflow; this scope revision does not change released contracts or other issues' requirements.

Keep the issue-linked planning identity `openspec/changes/gh-30-shared-monitoring-acceptance/`. Keep planning proportionate to this scope and record actual installation, client and physical results separately. Close this issue when the acceptance criteria above pass; deferred work does not keep it open.

## Owner scope revision

The user selected the existing Linux/WSL installation and explicitly chose a faster personal-project approach, accepting temporary breakage and repair instead of formal migration safety and rollback guarantees. This scope replaces the previous expanded acceptance criteria. No separate Linux upgrade prerequisite is required.

This tracker revision does not itself perform installation or operate the device. The installation and physical work follow as the next stage. Guide-source synchronization and public guide publication remain pending separately; this tracker-only revision changes neither.

title: Introduce device-aware Nanoleaf state and geometry contracts
body:
## Desired outcome

Let the Linux bridge state describe more than one Nanoleaf device without duplicating task ingestion or losing the existing Lines configuration. Establish the storage and geometry shape that the worker, renderers, and interfaces in [#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/42) and [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43) build on.

This is a personal project with one operator and one Linux installation. The issue is sized for that. It asks for a Linux-only schema change, a small device registry, and one migration test. It leaves out Windows compatibility, adapter layers, and a future allocation pool.

## Scope

A device is one physical Nanoleaf controller with its attached lights. An element is one physical Line or triangle. A zone is an independently controlled lighting part: a Line has two, a triangle has one. Each device owns its own placement and capacity; there is no separate pool concept in this version.

Shared data stays shared: task history, task IDs, project identity, task-project overrides, status epochs, and Codex unread evidence keep one owner. Device-scoped data gains a device column: slot assignments, project reservations, waiting state, modes, pending map edits, completion-effect state, and saved scenes.

Follow [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-linux-runtime-ownership.md) and the [Linux installation guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/linux-install.md). Runtime and private state live under `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf`. The existing worker remains the sole light writer.

Out of scope here:

- The legacy Windows installation. It keeps its current schema and is not migrated, adapted, or opened. No Windows fixtures or Windows-owned coordination.
- A compatibility adapter layer. Existing functions gain a device argument that defaults to the original Lines device.
- A pool identity separate from device identity. [#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/47) is deferred; a column can be added when it matters.
- Enabling personal hardware, reading NL22 layout, or rendering on Panels. [#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/42) owns runtime integration and [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43) owns NL22 geometry and effect payloads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: Task ingestion, task IDs, project identity, task-project overrides, status epochs, and Codex unread evidence keep one shared owner. Device-scoped rows reference that shared data rather than copying the task reducer.
- [ ] AC2: A device registry records id, kind (`lines` or `panels`), address, and token reference. Device identity survives a configured address change. Element identity is device-qualified, so equal panel IDs on two devices cannot collide. The original Lines device keeps the identity established by #28.
- [ ] AC3: Slot assignments, waits, comets, line preferences, display state, map settings, pending edits, locate, mode, and saved scene are keyed by device. Uniqueness becomes device plus slot, so one task can hold one placement on Lines and one on Panels.
- [ ] AC4: The layout file holds one entry per device. Each element carries its physical ID, its existing numbering, and a zone list: two for a Line, one for a triangle. Task assignment and map presentation read that shape rather than the Lines-only pairing. Initialization rejects a malformed layout and keeps the last valid one.
- [ ] AC5: Migration runs inside the existing Linux initialization as guarded column additions with default `lines`, and is idempotent. One fixture test opens a copy of a pre-change Linux database, runs initialization twice, and checks that tasks, project and half preferences, scene choice and brightness, an active comet, pending edits, and protected-API credentials and request history survive with their values and epochs intact.
- [ ] AC6: Callers with no device target continue to address the original Lines device. Existing Lines-only behavior, the Python suite, and browser checks pass unchanged apart from the new device parameter.
- [ ] AC7: A short ADR at the next unused number records device identity, device-scoped state, the Linux-only migration, and the deliberate omission of Windows support, adapters, and pools. Behavioral requirements go in the applicable specs with their guide links updated.

## Verification approach

Use one isolated Linux database fixture containing active tasks, unread completions, an active comet, pending edits, a saved scene, and protected-API history. Compare preserved values and epochs before and after migration and repeated initialization. Exercise equal panel IDs across two registry entries and an address change with fake addresses and no credentials. Run the full Python suite and the OpenSpec and workflow checks; run browser checks if the map's API changes. These checks use temporary state and fake transport.

## Dependencies

- #28 is satisfied: the protected controller API was delivered through PR #39, merged as 3c2911c3bdd32f69c39883a0253e78858afc19df. Refresh that baseline before implementation.
- Linux source support was delivered by [#54](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/54) through [PR #57](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/57). [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-linux-runtime-ownership.md) is the runtime ownership baseline.
- Next: [#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/42).

## Delivery target

Source-only foundation on the Linux runtime. The installation and physical trial with both Lines and Panels remain with [#46](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/46), whose Windows-specific criteria need reconciliation with ADR 0007 before that trial. This issue does not install or upgrade a personal runtime, change hooks or services, or operate lights.

## Planning and delivery

Source delivery follows AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md: an isolated issue branch, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews against the same committed comparison, required CI, guarded merge, and main-CI readback. UI changes require human approval of the current candidate.

The issue-linked planning root is `openspec/changes/gh-41-device-state-geometry/`. Check active and archived changes for this exact issue before creating or reusing it.

## Revision note

Scope reduced on 2026-09-22 for a single-operator Linux installation. The original body required legacy Windows migration and coordination, source compatibility adapters, a pool identity separate from device identity, and a fresh-versus-migrated verification matrix. I removed those. The edit history holds the prior text.

title: Run independent Lines and Light Panels projections in the Nanoleaf runtime
body:
## Desired outcome

Let the existing Python worker display the same eligible task activity on Lines and Light Panels while keeping placement, modes, effects, scenes, and failures independent for each device.

This is a personal project with one operator and one Linux installation. The issue is sized for that. It builds on the device registry and device-scoped state from [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41) and leaves out Windows compatibility, adapter layers, and a combined allocation pool.

## Scope

Consume the device registry, device-scoped tables, and layout shape from [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41). Integrate mirrored allocation, device-specific output scheduling, existing scene restoration, explicit CLI targeting, and multi-device use of the protected API delivered by #28. Use the existing Lines renderer and a fake second renderer here; [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43) supplies the real NL22 adapter.

Keep one ingestion path and the existing Python worker as the sole light writer. Follow [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-linux-runtime-ownership.md): hooks, CLI, wall map, controller, and worker coordinate through private Linux SQLite, and local MCP uses direct loopback HTTP.

The [hub architecture](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#ownership) assigns provider/session interpretation to the shared core and device projections to Nanoleaf. Keep allocation, effects, modes, scene restoration, and output scheduling in Nanoleaf. [#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29) owns shared-feed input; do not duplicate the shared reducer.

Out of scope here:

- The legacy Windows installation. It is not migrated, adapted, or tested. No Windows fixtures or forwarding coverage.
- A compatibility adapter layer. Callers with no device target address the original Lines device through the default device argument from #41.
- A combined allocation pool. [#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/47) is deferred.
- Shared monitoring migration, new MCP infrastructure, and new generic scene, brightness, power, zone, or preview commands.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: A working task can occupy one element on each device. Each device independently preserves valid assignments, project reservations, Shared overflow, capacity, and its waiting list. A full or failed device does not redistribute tasks to the other device.
- [ ] AC2: Completion/read evidence is shared, while completion queues, active source reservations, and pending display edits are device-scoped. Reading a completed task through existing Codex evidence clears its indications on both devices; the map/API never marks it read.
- [ ] AC3: Each device independently persists Work, Quiet, and Free and restores its own latest saved scene and brightness. A change affecting one device does not clear the other device's effects, pending edits, mode, or restoration state. Free makes no further device requests after successful handoff.
- [ ] AC4: Preserve two-second status epochs, the one outward pulse, red/yellow priority, and one completion comet per eligible completion per device. Entering Work, registering a device, and recovering a connection do not reset epochs or replay obsolete effects. New task-project overrides preserve affected active comet sources until their existing completion boundary.
- [ ] AC5: Catch failures and schedule bounded retries per device. A failing device cannot abort the other device's due updates or overwrite its last successful outcome. Preserve #28's hold on failed/uncertain machine requests: automatic retry must not replay them; a fresh explicit request is required.
- [ ] AC6: Add explicit device targeting to CLI mode/status controls. Existing commands with no target still address the original Lines device, regardless of registry order. An explicit Both devices operation makes two targeted requests and returns both outcomes, including partial success; it does not promise atomic physical effects.
- [ ] AC7: Protected discovery, snapshots, commands, revisions, request replay, feeds, and credential permissions distinguish devices. Preserve the existing Lines identity and existing credentials' target scope; registering a second device never silently broadens access. A request, replay, or revocation for one target cannot execute against the other.
- [ ] AC8: Retain the adopted shared wire contract and its mode-only capability scope. Compose Both devices from individually targeted operations rather than adding a bulk command to the shared schema. Keep authentication, origin/Host checks, time/queue bounds, and private destination registration.
- [ ] AC9: Snapshot/feed and cached display reads do not discover device geometry, allocate tasks, advance effects, send lights, or refresh device evidence by observation alone. The worker retains these responsibilities.

## Verification approach

Use fake clocks, isolated Linux task state, two fake devices, and a fake launcher. Cover mirroring, per-device overflow and reservations, mixed modes, source-preserving deferred edits, completion/read handling, outage/reconnect, partial Both devices outcomes, and no-replay across restart. Exercise equal request counters on different targets, stale commands, target-scoped permissions and discovery, revocation, and repeated reads. Run the Python suite, protected contract fixtures, browser checks for API changes, and OpenSpec/workflow checks. These source checks require no live installation.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41). Begin only after its registry and device-scoped state are delivered.
- Next: [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43). Coordinate compatibility with #29 and #33; neither is a prerequisite for this automatic task display path.

## Delivery target

Source-only runtime and interface integration on the Linux runtime. No personal configuration, hardware enrollment, installation, or physical-light operations. [#46](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/46) owns the later installed and physical trial with both Lines and Panels; reconcile its Windows-specific criteria with [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-linux-runtime-ownership.md) before that trial.

## Planning and delivery

Source delivery follows AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md: an isolated issue branch, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews against the same committed comparison, required CI, guarded merge, and main-CI readback. UI changes require human approval of the current candidate.

The issue-linked planning root is `openspec/changes/gh-42-independent-device-worker/`. Check active and archived changes for this exact issue before creating or reusing it.

## Work guide follow-up

Guide-source synchronization and public publication remain pending for #29, #42, and #43. The next authorized delivery or guide coordinator owns refreshing the affected Nanoleaf backlog inputs and narrative in a linked hub PR under the [shared guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md), followed by separately authorized publication and live verification.

## Revision note

Scope reduced on 2026-09-22 for a single-operator Linux installation, matching the same-day trim of #41. I removed legacy Windows forwarding coverage, Windows-to-Linux import language, the compatibility adapter framing, the combined pool reference, closed #55 references, and the standard-library legacy startup clause. The edit history holds the prior text.

title: Run Lines and NL22 Light Panels as independent devices in the Nanoleaf worker
body:
## Desired outcome

Let the existing Python worker display the same task activity on Lines and original triangular NL22 Light Panels. Each triangle shows one task with the bridge's colors and animations, and each device keeps its own placement, mode, effects, saved scene and failures.

This is a personal project with one operator and one Linux installation. The issue is sized for that. It absorbs the device-worker scope from [#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/42), which is closed in favor of this issue.

## Scope

Build on the device registry, device-scoped tables and layout shape delivered by [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41) in PR #65. The work has two parts:

1. **Device worker.** Mirrored per-device allocation, device-specific output scheduling, per-device mode and scene restoration, per-device failure isolation and explicit CLI targeting.
2. **NL22 renderer.** NL22 geometry interpretation and a payload renderer alongside the existing split-zone Lines renderer. Reuse HTTP custom-effect timelines instead of adding a streaming writer.

Keep one ingestion path, including the shared-input path from [#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29), and keep the existing Python worker as the only light writer. Follow [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-linux-runtime-ownership.md): hooks, CLI, wall map, controller and worker coordinate through private Linux SQLite, and local MCP uses direct loopback HTTP. Allocation, effects, modes, scene restoration and output scheduling stay in Nanoleaf; do not duplicate the shared reducer.

Close the known gaps [ADR 0009](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/decisions/0009-device-aware-state.md) assigned to #42, and update that ADR's gap paragraph to point here:

- The worker renders and applies mode changes for the original device only.
- Display-cache clears, `setup --reset` and shared-source switching clear every device.

The target reported by the user is model NL22, firmware 5.2.2, hardware 1.6.2. The supplied photo shows 18 triangles in three connected hexagons, with the center hexagon raised. Treat that as the expected arrangement, not verified panel identities. [#46](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/46) checks device-reported model, layout and physical orientation. Keep the configured address and original photo out of GitHub issue attachments and repository fixtures.

Out of scope here:

- A second device on the protected controller API, integration settings API or local MCP. Those keep addressing the original Lines device. Open a new issue if the hub UI later needs Panels over the API.
- A "Both devices" CLI operation. Run the targeted command once per device.
- The legacy Windows installation, its fixtures and its regression coverage.
- A compatibility adapter layer. Callers with no device target address the original Lines device through #41's default device argument.
- A combined allocation pool. [#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/47) is deferred.
- Shared monitoring migration and new MCP infrastructure.

## Acceptance criteria

### Device worker

- [ ] AC1: A working task can occupy one element on each device. Each device independently keeps valid assignments, project reservations, Shared overflow, capacity and its waiting list. A full or failed device does not redistribute tasks to the other device.
- [ ] AC2: Completion and read evidence is shared; completion queues, active source reservations and pending display edits are device-scoped. Reading a completed task through existing Codex evidence clears its indications on both devices. The map and API never mark a task read.
- [ ] AC3: Each device independently persists Work, Quiet and Free and restores its own latest saved scene and brightness across takeover, idle, Quiet, Free and recoverable failure. Quiet uses the existing steady 10 percent policy and Work keeps its brightness policy. A change affecting one device does not clear the other device's effects, pending edits, mode or restoration state. Free makes no further device requests after a successful handoff. Display-cache clears, `setup --reset` and shared-source switching affect only the device they target, or say explicitly that they reset all devices.
- [ ] AC4: Keep two-second status epochs, the one outward pulse, red/yellow priority and one completion comet per eligible completion per device. Entering Work, registering a device, recovering a connection, switching layouts and editing project colors do not reset epochs or replay obsolete effects. New task-project overrides keep affected active comet sources until their existing completion boundary.
- [ ] AC5: Catch failures and schedule bounded retries per device. A failing device cannot abort the other device's due updates or overwrite its last successful outcome.
- [ ] AC6: CLI mode and status controls accept an explicit device target. With no target they address the original Lines device regardless of registry order. An unknown target is rejected rather than falling back to Lines.
- [ ] AC7: The protected controller, integration settings API and local MCP keep addressing the original Lines identity only. The shared wire contract, capability declaration, snapshots, credentials and request replay are unchanged. #64's power, brightness and saved-scene overrides and #28's hold on failed or uncertain machine requests apply to Lines only and never write to Panels. Registering Panels does not change what any existing credential can do.

### NL22 renderer

- [ ] AC8: Read supported NL22 layout data into stable one-zone triangle elements, keeping panel identities, coordinates, orientation and neighboring geometry. Exclude non-light modules. Reject malformed or unsupported geometry instead of mapping it as Lines. Use reported geometry; do not assign real panel IDs from the photo.
- [ ] AC9: Generate valid HTTP custom and static effect payloads for NL22. Lines-specific paired-zone assumptions stay in the Lines renderer. Both renderers run under the existing worker, with one writer per physical device and independently addressed transport.
- [ ] AC10: Whole triangles show the existing working green, question yellow, blocked red and unread blue states, with the two-second pulse, one outward status wave and completion comet. Travel is calculated within that device's arrangement. Overlapping effects keep red/yellow alert priority and active source reservations.
- [ ] AC11: One triangle supplies one task slot. Project reservations apply per triangle and support selecting a six-triangle region through ordinary multi-selection. Project identity appears through reservations and the map; triangles do not pretend to have project/status halves. Lines keep their existing half behavior. Classic/Project allocation, Shared overflow, waiting tasks and idle baseline follow the selected device's existing policies.
- [ ] AC12: Explicit Locate targets the chosen physical triangle only, respects that device's Free mode and keeps the current completion-source rules. Ordinary selection and read requests do not send Locate or effects.
- [ ] AC13: A synthetic, anonymized 18-triangle fixture exercises the supplied topology without live IDs, credentials, raw device state, the original photo or private task data. Support valid reported counts instead of hard-coding 18. Existing Lines fixture and payload behavior remains covered.

Review rule, not a separate test target: snapshot, feed and cached display reads do not discover device geometry, allocate tasks, advance effects, send lights or refresh device evidence by observation alone. The worker keeps those responsibilities.

## Verification approach

Use fake clocks, isolated Linux task state, a fake Lines device, a fake NL22 device and a fake launcher. Cover mirroring, per-device overflow and reservations, mixed modes, deferred edits that keep their comet source, completion and read handling, outage and reconnect, and no replay across restart. Compare emitted NL22 payloads against documented custom-effect semantics: triangle geometry and orientation, one-zone count, overlapping status priority, waves and comets, Locate, invalid geometry and connection failure. Confirm the protected API fixtures are unchanged and that API requests never reach the Panels transport. Run the Python suite, protected contract fixtures, browser checks if API-visible geometry changes, and OpenSpec/workflow checks. Source tests establish payload and behavior evidence, not physical NL22 acceptance.

## Dependencies

- #41 is delivered (PR #65). Nothing blocks this issue.
- Next: [#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/44). Authoritative live rendering data and exact UI-to-light mirroring stay with #15 and #17 and do not block basic panel support.

## Delivery target

Source-only worker integration, NL22 renderer and synthetic fixtures on the Linux runtime. No personal configuration, hardware enrollment, installation or physical-light operations. [#46](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/46) owns the later installed and physical trial with both Lines and Panels, and that trial does not block source implementation.

## Reference

The [Nanoleaf Light Panels Open API documentation](https://nanoleaf.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/nlapid/pages/2789310530/Nanoleaf%2BLight%2BPanels%2BOpen%2BAPI%2BDocumentation) describes panel-level HTTP custom/static animation timelines. Refresh it for implementation-changing protocol details before delivery.

## Planning and delivery

Source delivery follows AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md: an isolated issue branch, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews against the same committed comparison, required CI, guarded merge and main-CI readback. UI changes require human approval of the current candidate.

The issue-linked planning root is `openspec/changes/gh-43-nl22-device-worker/`. Check active and archived changes for #42 or #43 before creating or reusing it. None existed on 2026-09-23.

The two parts can land as one PR or as two PRs against this issue, device worker first. Either way, the issue closes only when all criteria pass.

## Work guide follow-up

Guide-source synchronization and public publication remain pending for #29 and #43, which now includes #42. The next authorized delivery or guide coordinator owns refreshing the affected Nanoleaf backlog inputs and narrative in a linked hub PR under the [shared guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md), followed by separately authorized publication and live verification.

## Revision note

Rescoped on 2026-09-23. This issue absorbed #42's device-worker scope, and #42 is closed. Reductions from #42's text:

- The protected API, credentials and MCP stay Lines-only. This drops per-target discovery, snapshots, revisions, replay, feeds, credential scoping and revocation.
- The "Both devices" CLI operation is dropped.
- The read-only-observation criterion is now a review rule.

Per-device modes stay, because #41 already stores mode per device. The blocked label is removed: #41, its only prerequisite, is delivered. The edit history holds the prior text of both issues.
