title: Switch the wall map between Lines and Light Panels
body:
## Desired outcome

Let the existing wall map show and edit one Nanoleaf device at a time, with a selector that switches between the original Lines and the NL22 Light Panels.

This is a personal project with one operator and one Linux installation. The issue is sized for that. The Linux runtime has no tray, so this issue covers the browser map and its API only.

## Scope

Add a device selector to the existing map. The selected device drives the page: its layout, mode, layout settings, reservations, pending state and Locate. Lines keep their current presentation. NL22 triangles render as plain SVG triangles with static status colours, drawn from the cached geometry delivered by [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43). This is the existing Nanoleaf editor, not a new hub dashboard.

Out of scope here: showing both devices at once, a "Both devices" mode action, Prism styling or simulated pulse, wave and comet animation for triangles, a triangle assembly animation, the retired Windows tray, and a combined allocation pool ([#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/47) is deferred).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The map opens on Lines. A labelled selector lists the registered devices and switches the page to the chosen one. The selection is kept in the URL, so a reload stays on the same device. With only Lines registered, the page behaves as it does today.
- [ ] AC2: Device-scoped reads and actions (state, mode, layout settings, assignment and Locate) address the selected device. Project colours and task project assignment stay shared. Requests that name no device address Lines, so existing browser and CLI callers behave as before. Unknown devices are rejected rather than falling back to Lines. The protected controller API stays Lines-only per #43.
- [ ] AC3: For the selected device, the page shows its mode with Work/Quiet/Free controls, its pending state and last error, its reservations and its waiting count. Changing one device's mode leaves the other device's mode and saved scene alone.
- [ ] AC4: Triangles support selection, multi-selection, project reservation, Shared release, inspector information and Locate. Triangles are numbered in the order #43's geometry reader returns them. Split-half and half-swap controls are hidden for triangles, and the backend rejects those settings for one-zone elements. Lines keep them.
- [ ] AC5: Rotation and flip apply to the selected device and are saved per device.
- [ ] AC6: Existing protections hold. Selection, refresh and switching devices send no physical Locate or effect. Display reads use cached geometry. Request-origin and edit-token checks remain, and browser responses never include Nanoleaf credentials.
- [ ] AC7: Keyboard selection and focus, reduced motion and the existing supported viewport sizes work on the triangle view. The Lines assembly behaviour delivered by #38 is unchanged, and switching to Panels plays no assembly.
- [ ] AC8: Record explicit human approval of the current UI candidate before merge. Agent review and successful CI do not substitute for that approval; changed UI requires renewed approval.

## Verification approach

Use deterministic browser fixtures with Lines and #43's synthetic 18-triangle NL22 fixture. Cover switching and URL persistence, targeted actions on each device, rejection of unknown devices, the Lines default for untargeted calls, triangle selection, reservation and Locate, and rejected split-half settings. Assert that selection and switching send no Locate. Keep #38's browser checks passing. Run the Python, browser and OpenSpec/workflow suites. Personal installation remains separate.

## Dependencies

- [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43) is delivered. #38 is delivered and merged.
- Sequenced after [#46](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/46) by choice. The Panels were enrolled (#45) and trialled (#46, closed 2026-09-24) with CLI mode controls, so nothing here is blocked.
- #45 promises that enrollment needs no service restart. The selector must therefore read the device registry on each request, not once at map startup, or a newly enrolled device would not appear until the map service restarts. The running map currently caches only the Lines configuration (`wall_server.App.config`).
- #29 and #33 are related consumers, not prerequisites. Exact animation parity from #15 and #17 is not part of this completion gate.

## Delivery target

Source-only map and API changes with a human-approved UI candidate. Installing the updated map on the Linux runtime needs a separate explicit request.

## Long-term direction

On 2026-09-25 the owner set a long-term direction: a B.U.N.N.Y. interface with device pages and a group page that shows every device ([agent-device-hub#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271)). This story still shows one device at a time, and its scope and acceptance criteria are unchanged. Two implementation choices keep that path open. They are design notes, not acceptance criteria:

- Draw each device through one renderer that takes a device and its cached geometry, instead of branching the page on Lines versus Panels. A later page can then show several devices or reuse the art.
- Key the page's device-scoped state by device, so showing two devices later adds entries rather than changing the model. [#119](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/119), which moves the page's rebuild policy behind a view model, makes this easier if it lands first.

## Planning and delivery

Source delivery follows AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md: an isolated issue branch, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews against the same committed comparison, required CI, guarded merge, and main-CI readback. UI changes require human approval of the current candidate.

The issue-linked planning root is `openspec/changes/gh-44-wall-map-device-selector/`. Check active and archived changes for this exact issue before creating or reusing it.

## Revision note

Scope reduced on 2026-09-22 for a single-operator Linux installation, matching the same-day trim of #41 through #43.

Rewritten on 2026-09-23 as a device selector and moved after #46. I removed the side-by-side sections and their responsive stacking, the global count that deduplicated tasks across sections, the "Both devices" action, focus and selection kept across two sections, the six-triangle region case, the numbering scheme based on geometry and device identity, and the requirement that triangle animation in the map stay honest (triangles now show static colours). The edit history holds the prior text.

Update 2026-09-24: #46 is complete. Added the requirement to read the device registry per request, so enrollment keeps working without a map restart.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment for [agent-device-hub#252](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252) on 2026-09-25, from this story's text, comments and recorded dependencies. It adds only ratings the story did not already record; readiness, labels and status are unchanged.

- **Complexity: medium.** Device-scoped state and per-request registry reads in the map and API.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Both blockers are closed and the scope was trimmed through 2026-09-24.
- **Impact: medium.** Changes live map and API behavior.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

title: Enroll a second Nanoleaf device on the Linux runtime
body:
## Desired outcome

Provide a Linux command that adds NL22 Panels to the existing Lines installation without losing current state, and that starts the new device in Free so nothing lights up until the operator chooses.

This is a personal project with one operator and one Linux installation. The issue is sized for that. The Linux runtime has no backup, upgrade, or rollback mechanism, and this issue does not add one. If enrollment goes wrong, the recovery path is to re-run it or remove the device entry.

## Scope

Add an explicit enrollment command for the source delivered by [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41) and [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43), following [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-linux-runtime-ownership.md) and the [Linux installation guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/linux-install.md). All automated verification uses isolated Linux state fixtures. Publishing or delivering this source does not enroll the user's devices.

Out of scope here: the retired Windows installation and its installer, backup and rollback tooling, WSL forwarding, firmware updates, hook migrations, remote ingress, and new services.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: An explicit enrollment command obtains or accepts a private NL22 credential, verifies the reported model and layout, and registers a stable device identity in the #41 registry without running fresh setup, clearing tasks, replacing trusted hooks, or altering the existing Lines identity.
- [ ] AC2: Store device addresses, credentials, raw layout and state, and machine permissions only under the private Linux state directory. Credentials do not reach browser responses, repository fixtures, ordinary logs, or issue evidence.
- [ ] AC3: A newly enrolled Panels device starts in Free and sends no task effects until explicitly activated. Enrollment captures usable geometry without assigning real panel IDs from the photo. Activation does not replay historical waves or completion effects.
- [ ] AC4: Enrollment failure, repeated enrollment, and identity or address conflicts leave existing devices and shared tasks intact. Never silently redirect an existing stable identity. The protected controller API stays Lines-only per #43, so enrollment neither grants nor changes machine credentials. Cached geometry and persisted preferences remain usable when a device is unavailable.
- [ ] AC5: Enrollment tells the operator which user systemd units to restart, or restarts only this installation's own units when asked. It preserves listener configuration, trusted hooks, selected modes, reservations, and pulse and comet epochs across that restart.
- [ ] AC6: Update the bridge, development, Linux installation, and controller API guides with enrollment, activation, and removal commands. Distinguish source fixtures from actual installation and physical evidence.

## Verification approach

Use temporary Linux state directories containing Lines-only state and then two configured fake devices. Exercise successful, failed, and repeated enrollment, duplicate IDs, unchanged machine credentials, and device removal, with fake controller responses. Do not contact personal devices. Run the Python suite, browser checks for API compatibility, and OpenSpec/workflow checks.

## Dependencies

- No open blockers. It builds on [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41) and [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43) (which absorbed #42), both delivered. Until the wall map gains a device selector in [#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/44), the Panels are activated and controlled with the CLI `--device` target.
- Next: [#46](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/46).

## Delivery target

Source-only enrollment tooling with isolated Linux verification. The actual personal pairing, mode activation, and visible-light tests belong to [#46](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/46) and require a later explicit installation task.

## Planning and delivery

Source delivery follows AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md: an isolated issue branch, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, focused red/green checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews against the same committed comparison, required CI, guarded merge, and main-CI readback.

The issue-linked planning root is `openspec/changes/gh-45-nl22-enrollment/`. Check active and archived changes for this exact issue before creating or reusing it.

## Revision note

Scope reduced on 2026-09-22 for a single-operator Linux installation, matching the same-day trim of #41 through #44. The original body was a Windows story: install-modes.ps1 backup and upgrade, rollback to a legacy Lines projection, interrupted-migration recovery, and WSL forwarding. I removed all of that and retitled the issue. What remains is a Linux enrollment command, private credential storage, a Free-by-default start, and conflict handling. The edit history holds the prior text.

Update 2026-09-23: #42 was folded into #43, which keeps the protected API on Lines only. Target-permission language is removed from AC4, AC6 and verification.

Update 2026-09-23: reordered ahead of #44. Enrollment needs only #41 and #43, so #44 no longer blocks it; the map device selector now follows #46.

Update 2026-09-23 (delivery start): the planning root is renamed to `gh-45-nl22-enrollment` because the upgrade scope was removed. No existing change used either name.

title: Verify Lines and NL22 Panels together on the installed Linux runtime
body:
## Desired outcome

Confirm that Lines and original NL22 Light Panels display useful task status together on the existing Linux installation, operate independently, and restore their own scenes and brightness.

## Scope

One installation and everyday-use trial for one operator in Ubuntu WSL. Source prerequisites [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41), [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43), and [#45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/45) are delivered. The wall map remains Lines-only; use the CLI `--device` target for Panels until [#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/44).

A later explicit installation task must authorize the intended devices, installation update, and bounded light sequence. Updating this issue does not authorize installation, pairing, or device operation.

Use the existing private Linux installation and [Linux installation guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/linux-install.md). Never run fresh setup to update it. Updating installed source may require restarting affected processes; enrollment itself requires no service restart. No backup, upgrade, or rollback tooling is added here.

User-reported Panels hardware is NL22, firmware 5.2.2, hardware 1.6.2, with 18 triangles arranged as three connected hexagons and the middle hexagon raised. Treat this as an expectation to check against the device, not a source of panel identities. Obtain addresses and credentials from private configuration; keep the original photo private.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — Identify the trial: record the delivered source revision, confirm both intended device identities, and read the NL22 model, firmware, and layout. Check the expected triangle count and plausible physical arrangement using reported geometry and representative visible placement. Resolve a material mismatch before dependent tests; do not guess panel identities or change firmware.
- [x] AC2 — Update and enroll: update the existing Linux installation without fresh setup and enroll Panels in Free using the delivered command. Confirm existing Lines tasks, reservations and preferences remain available and normal task display through the existing input source still works. Keep the selected shared-monitoring source; do not switch back to legacy hooks for this trial. Preserve credentials and trusted hooks. Restart only processes needed for the source update; enrollment alone needs no restart.
- [x] AC3 — Check task display: use representative tasks and the existing synthetic effect previews to confirm a task appears once on each device, representative triangle placement makes sense, and shared completion/read evidence clears the corresponding indications on both. Observe working green, question yellow, blocked red, unread blue, a status pulse, an outward wave, and a completion effect. Confirm red/yellow alerts remain visible and Lines retain split-half behavior. This is a visual functional check, not precise timing or exhaustive transition testing. Do not mark Codex tasks read through the map or by editing Codex state.
- [x] AC4 — Check modes and restoration: briefly exercise Work, Quiet, and Free on each device. Confirm Quiet is steady at its intended brightness, changing one device's mode leaves the other alone, and each device restores its own saved scene and brightness at the agreed idle or Free boundary. Use targeted CLI commands for Panels; a full matrix of mixed-mode combinations is unnecessary.
- [x] AC5 — Check the existing map: confirm the wall map opens, still shows Lines, and one targeted Lines control works with Panels enrolled. Panels selection and triangle reservations remain outside this trial; the map selector follows in #44.
- [x] AC6 — Finish and record: keep the installed worker as the only light writer for each device throughout the trial. Restore the user-selected modes and scene preferences at the end. Record a concise result with the source revision, installation outcome, visible observations, scene restoration, final modes, and remaining problems. Separate transport acknowledgments from the user's visible-light confirmation. Exclude credentials, private addresses and paths, raw task/device data, and the original photo. Close only when the retained criteria pass and the user confirms the visible result; otherwise keep the issue open with the specific next action.

## Verification approach

Reuse source-test evidence from #41, #43, and #45. Perform the separately authorized installation and one bounded visual sequence, using synthetic tasks where possible, plus a normal task check through the installed shared-monitoring source. No new test harness, soak period, or production qualification exercise is required.

The NL22 payload version, logical-panel flag, and orientation semantics were left physically unconfirmed by [#43's delivery](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43#issuecomment-5789645955). Successful visible task placement and effects must establish that the delivered behavior works on this device; API acceptance alone is insufficient.

Out of scope for this completion gate: locating every Line, exhaustive capacity/waiting-list tests, precise optical timing, every animation/mode transition, deliberate outage injection, reconnect/restart matrices, uncertain machine-request replay testing, firmware qualification, Windows support, rollback tooling, and exact UI-to-light frame synchronization. Record and investigate failures encountered during ordinary use; do not silently waive a failed retained criterion.

## Dependencies and next action

- No open source blockers. #41 and #43 are closed; #45 was delivered in [PR #79](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/79) and closed on 2026-09-23.
- Installation and visible-light trial completed with the operator on 2026-09-24 UTC. See the acceptance receipt below. Final modes: Lines Work, Panels Free with their saved scene and brightness restored.
- Use `blocked` only when a concrete required dependency, decision, or verification is unavailable, and state the obstacle and next action. An unscheduled trial alone is not a source blocker.
- #44 follows this trial by choice and does not block it. #47 remains future work.
- #34 owns local MCP acceptance; #30 owns shared-monitoring migration. This trial does not wait for #29 or #33. #15 and #17 retain authoritative rendering and exact parity scope.

## Delivery target

Installed and visibly confirmed behavior, not another source implementation project. A successful trial needs a concise acceptance comment; source delivery alone cannot close this issue.

If the trial discovers a source defect, scope the repair and follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md, including applicable planning, tests, independent review, CI, and PR delivery. UI changes require approval of the current candidate. Those repair steps are conditional on an actual source change.

## Revision note

Reduced to a personal-project installation and everyday-use trial. Removed the satisfied #45 blocker and changed backlog status to ready while retaining the hardware label and explicit operation-authorization boundary. The earlier Linux-only and CLI-first decisions remain; the edit history preserves the previous nine-criterion scope. Deferred regression exercises are not prerequisites for this issue's completion.

title: Combine Lines and Light Panels into one layout and allocation pool
body:
## Desired outcome

Eventually present Lines and Light Panels as one spatial layout and allocate each task once across a shared pool of their elements, replacing mirrored placement when that combined pool is selected.

This is the Nanoleaf part of a wider pool. On 2026-09-25 the owner asked for a task pool that any device can join or leave, including the Pixoo and LIFX bulbs ([agent-device-hub#272](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/272)). Design this pool with the membership model decided there, so adding other devices later extends it rather than replacing it. In Work, the operator should be able to choose the Lines alone, the Panels alone, both mirrored, or both extended. The first two already work by putting the other device in Free or Quiet.

## Scope

Record the future direction requested alongside the first mirrored-device release. Reuse stable device and element identity, one shared task owner, and the existing worker as the only light writer from [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41) and [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43). #41 keys placement by device and adds no separate pool identity; this design decides whether a pool column is needed. The verified mirrored configuration remains available as a baseline.

This issue is deferred design work. Do not enable a combined pool, redistribute tasks, invent placement rules, or mark it ready as part of the initial NL22 delivery. The user has chosen the eventual outcome; the behavior below still requires a focused design discussion.

## Decisions required before implementation readiness

- Decide how the two physical arrangements appear in one canvas, including their relative position, scale, orientation, and whether placements represent physical distance or a chosen logical arrangement. The B.U.N.N.Y. group page ([agent-device-hub#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271)) needs the same decision, so make it once.
- Decide how a device joins and leaves the pool, using agent-device-hub#272's membership model, and what happens to its placed tasks when it leaves.
- Decide allocation priority, project reservations, Shared overflow, capacity reporting, and element selection across one-zone triangles and two-zone Lines. Define what one task placement means without duplicating that task across the combined pool.
- Decide eligibility when devices have independent Work, Quiet, and Free modes or are unavailable, including whether and when tasks can move, and how existing reservations and active comet sources are preserved.
- Decide whether waves and comets stay within a device or cross the combined layout, and specify the timing and failure behavior without assuming synchronized transport or exact optical parity.
- Define opt-in migration from mirrored assignments that preserves tasks, unread evidence, preferences, and effect epochs, and whether a way back to mirrored placement is worth building for one operator. Identify any required API or renderer changes using the existing shared ownership boundaries.

## Acceptance criteria for the design phase

- [ ] AC1: After [#46](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/46), resolve the decisions above with the user and record observable allocation, layout, mixed-mode, outage, animation, and migration scenarios.
- [ ] AC2: The accepted design provides one task placement across the selected combined pool while keeping physical device identity and device ownership explicit. It does not duplicate provider interpretation or introduce a second writer.
- [ ] AC3: Assign settled requirements, lasting decisions, and delivery scope to the repository's existing specification, ADR, and GitHub owners. Define implementation issue boundaries and dependencies rather than silently expanding the completed initial release.
- [ ] AC4: Specify deterministic allocation and migration tests, browser cases and human UI approval, and separately authorized physical verification for any changed device behavior. Exact synchronization claims need their own evidence consistent with #15 and #17.
- [ ] AC5: Keep status:backlog and deferred until the required decisions and prerequisites are settled. Do not treat the first mirrored release or this ticket's existence as acceptance of a combined-pool implementation.

## Verification approach

The initial deliverable is a reviewed, decision-complete design with testable examples covering the decisions above. No source tests, UI candidates, or device operations are claimed by this backlog definition. Later implementation must follow the repository's normal source, UI, installation, and physical evidence gates.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by [#46](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/46) and unresolved design choices. The first release must establish verified independent control before combined-pool migration is designed for delivery.
- Reuse foundations from [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41) and [#43](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/43); coordinate with #15 and #17 when defining renderer and timing implications. Shared monitoring and MCP infrastructure remain with their existing issues.

## Delivery target

title: Expose connector geometry for the Prism wall map
body:
## Desired outcome

The wall map can place crystal tubes against the flat faces of the actual hexagonal connectors, using validated layout data and the existing physical Line identities.

## Scope

Extend the existing geometry cache and wall-state projection with a small, versioned connector and Line-end contract. This is the geometry prerequisite for the approved Prism UI integration.

At planning baseline `ea3b95661352f927aceaf92b62d74660978c201f`, `bridge/wall_server.py:ensure_geometry` retains only shapeType 18 zone positions and skips refresh when that cache exists. `project_map.geometry` exposes three points per Line, not exact connector centers. A raw-layout fixture alone therefore does not establish that an existing cache supplies the required information.

Preserve connector centers, source identities, endpoint relationships, and orientation through the existing backend owner. Keep `line_groups` order, `project_map.line_id`, physical numbering, and the two zone IDs in their current order. Define where orientation, Y inversion, rotation, and flips apply so each transform runs once.

This work covers current Lines with six-face hexagonal connectors. It does not add Light Panels, 90-degree connectors, multi-device allocation, a second state owner, a new controller API, or light writes. It does not migrate Windows installation data. The separately planned fresh Linux installation reuses this wall server and UI; coordinate overlapping geometry/cache changes without making that service move a prerequisite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: A credential-free, versioned geometry projection identifies connector centers, the connector at each Line end, stable Line IDs/numbers, and ordered zone IDs. Duplicate controller entries at one housing retain source identity without rendering duplicate housings. Existing wall-state fields and callers continue working.
- [x] AC2: A fresh layout and an existing zone-only cache both obtain connector geometry through the designated backend path. Enrichment preserves existing tasks, reservations, preferences, assignments, scenes, and epochs. It requires no fresh setup, Windows process launch, browser device request, or additional light writer.
- [x] AC3: Invalid, incomplete, unsupported, or unavailable layout data cannot replace the last valid geometry or fabricate a connection. With no exact connector data, the existing wall remains usable through a documented fallback and bounded retry. Concurrent readers cannot observe a partially replaced cache. Geometry reads do not create continuous device polling in Free mode or requests tied to animation frames.
- [x] AC4: The saved 15-Line layout and synthetic chain, branch, cycle, and disconnected fixtures preserve topology, relative lengths, Line identity, and zone ownership across global orientation, map rotations, and flips. Where two controller IDs describe one connector housing, they resolve consistently. The renderer can derive flat-face joins without rounding visible Line endpoints into guessed connector centers.
- [x] AC5: The new geometry fields contain only the data needed for drawing. They exclude tokens, device addresses, configuration objects, local paths, and task metadata. Existing Host, origin, authentication, and response restrictions remain effective; this issue does not widen the protected machine API.
- [x] AC6: Document the geometry contract, compatibility behavior, cache owner, and transform convention for the renderer. Link issue-specific OpenSpec scenarios to these criteria. Reconcile with any intervening device-geometry or Linux-runtime changes before selecting the final schema.

## Verification approach

All checks below are planned, not executed by issue publication.

| Criteria | Planned evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC1, AC4 | Isolated producer/consumer fixtures asserting exact IDs, numbering, zone order, connector centers, transforms, and topology; browser smoke check against the existing map. |
| AC2, AC3 | Fresh and legacy cache fixtures, repeated enrichment, simultaneous reads, malformed/missing connector entries, timeout/failure and recovery. Snapshot application state before/after and count fake device calls, including repeated Free-mode reads. |
| AC5 | Privacy canaries in backend-only configuration and metadata; assert absence from the new projection. Exercise rejected Host/origin requests and existing protected-write tests. |
| AC6 | Contract/specification review against current main and the accepted renderer inputs. |

Run `python3 scripts/check.py` and `npm run test:browser` for the API change. After applicable OpenSpec changes and `npm ci`, run `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow`. Use synthetic state and fake lights. These checks do not establish installation or physical-light acceptance.

## Dependencies and scope references

- No unfinished feature prerequisite. Ready for separately authorized source delivery.
- Preserve [Line identification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/openspec/specs/wall-line-identification/spec.md) and the [bridge behavior contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/bridge/README.md).
- Coordinate schema changes with [device-aware geometry #41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/41); it is related work, not a required multi-device implementation.
- Exact physical-frame mirroring remains [#15](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/15) and [#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17). Shared-frontend configuration remains [#49](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/49).

## Assessment

Planning, 2026-09-09, source baseline above.

- Complexity: medium. Cache acquisition, validation, transforms, and the browser projection must agree while retaining existing callers.
- Uncertainty: medium. The bounded investigation is to derive endpoint relationships and shared housings from sanitized controller fixtures, then prove an additive contract against old and new caches before renderer integration. Unsupported geometry must produce an explicit fallback.
- Impact: high. The geometry response is derived from credential-bearing configuration and cache writes share a boundary with application preferences. Privacy and preservation checks are required even though the intended feature is visual.
- Readiness: ready. Product decisions are settled; the bounded contract investigation is part of this item. Reassess if #41 or the Linux move changes ownership/schema, or fixtures cannot establish endpoint relationships.

## Delivery target and handoff

Source-only. Publication starts no implementation, installation, service, hook, or device operation.

Future delivery uses the current SDLC, an owned isolated worktree, the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change, and independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed candidate. Review the response/cache boundary for privacy and concurrent reads. Any visible fallback change also requires human approval of the current UI candidate before merge.

The source-delivery coordinator owns contract handoff to the Prism renderer and coordination with Linux packaging. Shared guide synchronization is pending: the authorized follow-up must update the affected backlog facts and `docs/work-guide/updates.md` through a linked Hub companion PR under the [guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md). This tracker publication does not publish repository PRs or the public guide.

title: Integrate Prism crystal artwork and two-zone wall animation
body:
## Desired outcome

Replace the wall's current artwork with the approved Prism crystal finish and a layout-driven mechanical assembly. The moving UI must use the same detailed components as the finished artwork, with bright cores and diffuse light spilling beyond the crystal.

## Scope and accepted decisions

Integrate the existing Prism finish kit into the current browser wall map. The separately planned Linux installation retains that UI, so reuse the existing application operations and make the assets portable with the wall server. No Windows tray artwork, tray animation, Windows Forms, service migration, or installation work is included.

The source reference is the owner-provided `prism-finish-kit.zip`, verified during planning with SHA-256 `ceef5c07993fa3aba77daae02521747fbb55d1c8595002231a378d06105f8fb0`. Its `INTEGRATION.md`, `prism.js`, `adapters.js`, component assets, layout fixtures, and exports are the implementation handoff. Round nine is the clean-start motion reference; the finish kit supplies the polished material. Import the selected reusable sources and reproducible asset build through this delivery's PR. Do not depend at runtime on a personal artifact directory. Confirm the matching archive is available before asset work; an unavailable archive blocks visual acceptance, not permission to invent replacements.

The approved UI rhythm is two seconds. Physical light behavior and timing remain unchanged. The kit's 2.6-second cycle, global light mode, single-selection model, disabled interaction during assembly, and controller-first root choice require adaptation to existing app behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: Render thicker faceted crystal tubes with a bold, bright core, long visible tail, and broad diffuse spill near the approved finish kit's upper glow range. Preserve crisp bevels and a hexagonal central connector. Tubes meet the flat faces of connectors. Static and animated poses use the same scalable material components and app-resolved colors; no screenshot replacement or fixed demo shape.
- [x] AC2: Each connector and Line can animate independently around its connection. From the existing most-connected hub selection, all hub-connected Lines begin together; tubes eject at full thickness and rotate with their connector into position, then assembly proceeds outward. The hub rotates with its attached structure. Other connectors grow from the arriving Line tip and unfold their six permanent inner-border sections clockwise or counterclockwise. No temporary triangle-to-border swap, thin white completion flash, lingering center shutter, or translucent overlay remains. Preserve the existing approximately two-second assembly, independent disconnected components, and exact final positions, including cycle-closing Lines.
- [x] AC3: Each Line retains two independently colored zones with stable endpoint ownership. During Work, every Line carrying a working, question, blocked, or unread task sends two bright packets from its connectors inward in one direction, meeting in a brief center spark within a two-second cycle. Idle Lines stay steady. Quiet is steady with reduced glow; Free is dim/desaturated with the released-state readout. Reduced motion skips assembly and suppresses travel and sparks while keeping modes distinguishable. Preserve red/yellow alerts, project signatures, half swaps, and completion semantics.
- [x] AC4: On first assembly completion, explicit Replay completion, or immediate completion caused by interaction, the UI flow begins at phase zero at both connectors after the structure is in place, when Work/task state permits flow. All active Lines share that phase. Polls, palette changes, selection, mode changes, focus, and reconnects do not randomly offset Lines, replay assembly, or reset the established UI clock. Preserve the page-wide phase across render rebuilds within the existing 50 ms boundary. Keep UI assembly/flow clocks separate from physical task pulse/comet epochs.
- [x] AC5: Preserve opening and map-entry preferences as separate browser-local toggles, existing defaults, and manual Replay. Interaction during assembly completes it immediately and then performs the intended action. Repeated Replay never queues. Geometry changes or connection failures end assembly immediately; the wall settles into the latest polled state with task lists, alerts, and connection information visible. Visibility pause/resume retains the current animation position.
- [x] AC6: Preserve stable Line numbering and IDs, Ctrl/Cmd/Shift multi-selection, keyboard focus, task/project/inspector associations, selection and pending rings, and existing mode controls. Selection, highlighting, animation, and Replay issue no write or Locate request. They do not mark tasks read, change assignments/scenes, mutate reservations, or restart completed effects. `settings.style` remains the existing Classic/Project allocation choice. Luminous-number visibility and collision changes belong to #26; retain current identification until that refinement lands.
- [x] AC7: Use the prerequisite geometry response to draw the saved 15-Line arrangement plus chain, branch, cycle, disconnected, and rotated/flipped fixtures. Malformed or unsupported geometry leaves a usable documented fallback and preserves the last valid layout. Surviving IDs retain selection and current colors through valid geometry replacement. Do not silently claim support for Light Panels, 90-degree connectors, or a 300-Line performance envelope.
- [x] AC8: Serve or build the selected local components through bounded asset paths with correct MIME types. Preserve Host/origin protections and the existing CSP; no arbitrary file server, remote asset dependency, or credential exposure. Verify the packaged wall can run through a foreground Linux server without Windows helpers. Coordinate the asset inclusion list with the Linux installation owner when that work is published, without taking ownership of service setup.
- [x] AC9: Dispose listeners, observers, and animation frames when a renderer is replaced or removed. Hidden hosts/documents pause motion; Quiet, Free, and reduced-motion steady states do not keep an unnecessary animation loop. Repeated state updates and view mounts do not multiply renderers or timers. Capture desktop/mobile and high-DPI visual evidence and frame measurements for the actual 15-Line layout and a documented larger synthetic fixture. Human approval of this implementation's current candidate establishes the final material/motion quality.

## Verification approach

All checks below are planned, not executed by issue publication. The kit's recorded preview checks are reference evidence, not app acceptance.

| Criteria | Planned evidence |
| --- | --- |

title: Support a fresh Linux installation of the Nanoleaf services
body:
## Outcome

Run the Nanoleaf worker, SQLite database, wall map, controller API, and MCP host in Ubuntu WSL on the existing PC. Reuse the separate processes and existing single light writer. Support Codex Desktop tasks executing in WSL and WSL CLI sessions.

This is a fresh install. Existing Nanoleaf data need not be imported or preserved. Preserve unrelated applications, hooks, and Codex data. Windows Desktop/browser clients and mounted JSON metadata reads remain supported.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A1. Provide a Linux setup command using a Python virtual environment and the existing Node MCP host. Accept device configuration privately and create runtime state under `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf` with owner-only permissions. No runtime SQLite database resides under `/mnt/c`; credentials stay out of Git and browser responses.
- [x] A2. Reuse the existing hook, CLI, wall-map, controller, and worker processes. All state coordination happens within Linux. Concurrent requests retain the existing worker lock and produce only one light writer.
- [x] A3. Register Linux hook commands while preserving unrelated hooks. Support WSL task execution and the existing configurable Desktop project, title, and unread JSON readers.
- [x] A4. Provide configurable loopback ports, defaulting to wall map `8765`, controller `41231`, and MCP `41230`. Add a command that prints the map URL without launching a browser. Port conflicts return useful errors.
- [x] A5. Configure MCP to use the existing direct HTTP controller transport. Preserve authentication, request identities, revision checks, and Work/Quiet/Free behavior. Linux runtime commands never launch Windows executables.
- [x] A6. Supply user systemd units for the wall map, controller, and MCP host, plus foreground commands. Keep the worker on demand. Document that availability follows WSL's lifetime.
- [x] A7. Update installation instructions, applicable ownership contracts, and issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts with a design and ownership ADR. Link the Hub documentation companion PR and state whether guide synchronization is complete or pending.

## Verification

The table below defines the required checks. Completed source evidence is recorded in the closing receipt and PR #57; installed and physical evidence remains #55.

| Criteria | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| A1, A3 | Fresh setup in temporary Linux state using fake device transport; verify private state placement and permissions, supplied device configuration, Linux hook registration, preservation of unrelated hooks, and configured metadata readers with available and unavailable fixtures. |
| A2 | Concurrent hook, CLI, map, and controller activity using isolated SQLite; verify that the existing lock admits only one light-writing worker. Retain rendering, unread, reservation, effect-epoch, and scene-behavior regressions. |
| A4 | Listener tests on configured loopback ports, actionable occupied-port failures, and URL-only output without browser or Windows process launch. Preserve map Host/Origin/edit-token checks. |
| A5 | Authenticated controller and MCP protocol tests against fake transport, including invalid credentials, duplicate/stale requests, and failure uncertainty. Inspect and exercise the Linux path without Windows forwarding. |
| A6 | Exercise foreground service commands and inspect unit entrypoints against the installed layout. Actual systemd operation belongs to installed acceptance. |
| A7 | Review the ownership decision, OpenSpec scenarios, setup/operation instructions, and companion PR against these criteria. |

Run `python3 scripts/check.py`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run test:mcp`, `npm run check:workflow`, and `npm run test:workflow` after their documented prerequisites, including root and MCP dependency installation. Preserve applicable hosted CI and independent Standards and Specification reviews. Reviews must cover credential boundaries and competing writers. Human approval remains required if the wall-map presentation changes.

## Dependencies and delivery boundary

Coordination and architecture documentation: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/43

Reuse the delivered controller API at https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28 and MCP bindings at https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/33. Both have merged source and recorded source acceptance. This issue does not wait for Hub #43 to close; its companion documentation can be prepared alongside implementation.

Installed acceptance: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/55. Source delivery does not install services, modify personal hooks, retire Windows processes, or operate lights.

Before implementation, prepare the exact `gh-54-linux-fresh-install` OpenSpec change, following AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. Deliver through an isolated worktree and reviewed PR.

The broader persistent-display requirements in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/11 remain separate. This issue covers only the Linux port and URL behavior needed here. Exclude data migration, rollback tooling, a combined daemon, a new hook API, Docker, native Windows task monitoring, shared monitoring, additional device support, and visual redesign. Leave unused Windows source alone unless a focused compatibility change is required.

## Planning assessment

Assessed 2026-09-09 against Nanoleaf main `ea3b95661352f927aceaf92b62d74660978c201f` and Hub main `2564a357ec7d1a72c5525c0f36b98287244a6e89`.

- Complexity: medium. Several existing interfaces need Linux installation and startup wiring. Linux process-launch support, the SQLite worker lock, and direct HTTP MCP transport already exist.
- Uncertainty: medium. The installed WSL hook environment, service manager access, and browser reachability require installed verification. Temporary-state source tests do not establish these claims.
- Impact: high. Credentials and device-writer ownership require review even for a home application.
- Readiness: ready for source work. Product decisions and source prerequisites are settled; installed claims remain separate.
- Reassess if Linux hook execution cannot access its state or launch the worker, ownership assumptions fail, or the scope/base changes materially. Do not silently introduce the excluded daemon or hook API as a workaround.

The complete fresh-install effort is estimated at 2–4 focused engineering days, excluding review and scheduling delays. This is the overall estimate, not an additional estimate for each linked issue. No implementation or operational work has started through this issue definition.

title: Install and verify the Linux Nanoleaf runtime in WSL
body:
## Outcome

Install the Linux Nanoleaf runtime in Ubuntu WSL on the existing PC and confirm the panels react to a real Codex task. This is a personal setup. Downtime is fine, and one closing comment is the acceptance record.

## Steps

- [x] 1. Stop this project's Windows worker, wall map, controller, MCP and tray. Disable its Startup entries and remove its old Nanoleaf hooks from the Codex home. Leave unrelated applications, hooks and Codex data alone.
- [x] 2. From the reviewed checkout at `2558df5a2fc543247b0c75898ef0260ba3ea264b` or later main, run `python3 bridge/install_linux.py --ip <device>` with `--hooks-file` pointing at the real Codex hooks file. Enter the token at the hidden prompt.
- [x] 3. Start the wall map, controller and MCP services. Use `systemctl --user` if it works from the WSL terminal, otherwise run the three foreground commands from the install doc in a tmux session.
- [x] 4. Run one Codex task in WSL and confirm the panels change. Run `nanoleaf mode work`, `quiet` and `free` from the CLI and confirm the panels follow. End in Free.
- [x] 5. Post one comment with the installed revision, what lit up and what did not, then close this issue.

## Rules that still matter

- Windows and Linux workers must never control the device at the same time. Step 1 comes before step 3.
- Keep the SQLite state on ext4, never under `/mnt/c`. The installer refuses mounted paths.
- Keep the device token out of command arguments, screenshots and this issue.

## Deferred

These are not required to close this issue. Open a follow-up if any of them turns out to matter.

- Service restart and startup-after-reopening-WSL checks. Availability follows WSL's lifetime, which the install doc already states.
- Authenticated MCP status and mode verification. Do it when mode commands from inside Codex are next wanted.
- Desktop title metadata from the mounted Codex JSON. Missing titles are a later bug, not a gate.
- Wall map reachability from the Windows browser. Worth a ten-second look, not a gate.
- Separate service, client, transport and visible-light evidence records.
- Independent Standards and Specification review. This issue produces no source change.

## References

- Install procedure: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/2558df5a2fc543247b0c75898ef0260ba3ea264b/docs/linux-install.md
- Source delivery, complete: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/54 (PR #57, merged as `2558df5a2fc543247b0c75898ef0260ba3ea264b`)
- Hub architecture and guide: https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/43. That issue should close on its documentation work and not wait on this one.

Backups, data migration, rollback tooling, a soak period, Windows keepalive or startup automation, native Windows task monitoring and unrelated data cleanup remain out of scope. Old Nanoleaf data may stay on disk unused.

Scope reduced 2026-09-22 to match a personal project. The earlier six-criterion body with its evidence table is in this issue's edit history.

title: Expose native power, brightness and saved-scene controls through the protected controller API
body:
## Outcome

Advertise and execute power, brightness and saved-scene activation as supported controller v1 capabilities on the protected controller API, so the shared BUNNY frontend can offer Nanoleaf general controls without an agent session.

## Scope and accepted definition

The accepted general-control definition is [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31), recorded in the hub as ADR 0005 (`docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md`). Released controller v1 already carries `power.set`, `brightness.set` and `scene.activate` in its closed command union, so no shared contract release is needed. The installation's single worker remains the only light writer. Work, Quiet and Free keep their native meanings; there is no global mode.

## Accepted behavior

- Power and brightness are mode-independent: the controller accepts them in Work, Quiet and Free.
- A brightness command is a user override. It persists until the next explicit mode command, which reapplies that mode's brightness policy. This issue owns the exact policy text, including how Work and Quiet effects render while brightness is overridden.
- The controller discovers the device's saved scene identities and advertises them through the `scenes` capability, bounded to 256 IDs. If scene display names are exposed, they travel through the `nanoleaf.integration` extension as user-chosen names from the Nanoleaf app. Nothing else is copied into labels.
- Scene activation is accepted only in Free. In Work or Quiet the command returns a typed v1 failure before any device write, reusing an existing failure code; no new wire value is introduced.
- Scene activation in Free is a one-shot worker write. It starts no polling, and Free continues to perform no controller polling after handoff. Task and effect epochs are preserved.
- Desired power and brightness become known after acceptance. Observed values stay unknown unless the worker holds evidence. Missing evidence is never fabricated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** The capability declaration marks `power`, `brightness` and `scenes` supported with typed constraints while `media`, `zones` and `preview` stay unsupported. All 220 shared fixture cases still pass. A linked Hub companion PR updates the hub's pinned Nanoleaf fixtures and compatibility record.
- [ ] **AC2.** `power.set` and `brightness.set` execute through the existing worker queue with the replay, revision, generation, uncertain-hold and single-writer rules delivered by #28.
- [ ] **AC3.** The brightness override policy above is specified and tested across Work, Quiet and Free transitions, including an override followed by a same-mode command.
- [ ] **AC4.** `scene.activate` uses discovered scene IDs, is accepted only in Free, returns a typed failure otherwise, performs one write with no follow-up polling and preserves epochs.
- [ ] **AC5.** Snapshots keep desired, pending, last successful send, last outcome and observation separate; unknown observation remains unknown.
- [ ] **AC6.** The legacy Windows bridge, tray, wall editor and hooks are unaffected; the full regression and browser suites pass. The exact issue-linked OpenSpec change named after this issue records the protected-controller-api delta.

Physical acceptance on the installed wall belongs to the separate hub hardware issue created by #31's decomposition. Source tests do not establish visible light output.

## Required source prerequisites

- [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31): general-control definition, accepted 2026-09-22.
- [#28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28): protected controller API, closed.

Coordinate shared-file changes under `bridge/` with the owner of the concurrent device-aware contracts work in #41. That work is not a required input here.

## Verification

Use fake device transports, disposable state and the shared contract fixtures. Cover accepted and rejected scene commands per mode, brightness override persistence and reapplication, uncertain transport holds, replay of identical requests and snapshot separation. Real client, installed runtime and visible-light evidence stay in the hardware issue.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-22, against codex-nanoleaf `main` and the accepted Hub #31 decisions.

- **Complexity: medium.** Worker queue, mode policy and scene discovery interact, but the queue and guards already exist.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The behavior is accepted; the remaining brightness policy text is a bounded refinement owned here.
- **Impact: medium.** Incorrect writes affect the physical wall; the single-writer, hold and replay rules bound recovery.

**Readiness:** ready for issue-linked specification and implementation. **Review:** independent Standards and Specification reviews plus concurrency review of the mode/override interaction. **Reassessment triggers:** changed scope, a scene discovery limitation found during implementation, or blocking review findings.

## Planning and delivery

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. Before behavior changes, create the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change and proportionate executable checks. Use isolated work, independent review, guarded merge and merged-revision CI. Keep credentials, private paths, agent content and runtime state out of Git. This issue does not authorize installation, device operations or settings changes.

title: Align guide-maintenance rules with the current hub procedure
body:
## Problem

`AGENTS.md` ("Work guide maintenance") and `docs/sdlc.md` still require every authorized delivery to coordinate a linked hub PR that records the delivery in `docs/work-guide/updates.md` or records a no-impact reason, and they treat guide synchronization as pending until that PR merges. The hub procedure changed in agent-device-hub #169 (`ad5aef8`, current `origin/main` `a76b22d`). It retires the `updates.md` ledger and requires a hub PR only when the authorized scope includes a guide update. Coordinators and reviewers now get conflicting instructions on every delivery. #68 / PR #69 hit this.

## Outcome

This repository's guide-maintenance rules match the hub's current procedure.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `AGENTS.md`, `docs/sdlc.md`, and the PR template no longer require an `updates.md` entry or a hub PR for every delivery. They point to the hub procedure and state when a linked hub PR is required.
2. `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` pass.

## Planning

Documentation maintenance with no behavior delta, so no OpenSpec change is needed.

title: Stale shared approval evidence keeps two Nanoleaf Lines red
body:
## Observed and expected behavior

On the existing Linux/WSL installation, the user observed two Nanoleaf Lines remaining red. Red is the documented indicator for a task blocked on input or approval ([bridge behavior](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/bridge/README.md#questions-blocks-and-read-status)). The selected shared-session feed continues to arrive, yet two assigned task records remain `blocked` with uncertain freshness and old approval attention. This can leave a red indicator in place without current evidence that an approval is still pending.

Expected: a genuinely pending approval remains red. Once reliable evidence says that approval was resolved, the corresponding Line leaves red. If the source cannot establish the current state, the product should expose that uncertainty and provide an evidence-based recovery path; it must not silently treat an old approval as confirmed current or clear a real pending approval merely because time passed.

## Reproduction and evidence (2026-09-23 UTC)

Read-only inspection of `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf/status.sqlite` using SQLite `mode=ro`, `PRAGMA query_only=ON`, and a read transaction found:

- Shared input selected; collector `running`; feed received about 0.5 seconds before inspection; snapshot revision 708, loss count 0.
- Five `blocked` session records, two with assigned Lines. The assigned records were in slots **4 and 13** and both appeared in `shared_stale`.
- In the corresponding feed records, both were Codex Desktop sessions with `freshness=uncertain`, `activity=unknown`, `read=unknown`, and an `approval` attention marker. Both carried unavailable evidence for ordering, attention, turn, and activity (ambiguous or missing). Their observation ages were roughly 2.8 hours. The local `waits` table had zero rows; shared-session attention is the relevant input here.
- A focused read-only assertion for assigned, blocked, stale records returned `[(4,), (13,)]` twice, three seconds apart. The feed revision was 703 during that repeat check and later advanced to 708, while the two assigned records remained blocked and stale.

Reproduction command for the local projection (no light request or state write):

```bash
python3 -c 'import sqlite3; d=sqlite3.connect("file:/home/jimmie/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf/status.sqlite?mode=ro",uri=True); d.execute("PRAGMA query_only=ON"); d.execute("BEGIN"); x=d.execute("SELECT slot FROM slots JOIN sessions ON slots.session=sessions.id JOIN shared_stale ON slots.session=shared_stale.session WHERE sessions.status=\"blocked\" ORDER BY slot").fetchall(); print(x); assert x==[(4,),(13,)]'
# Observed: [(4,), (13,)]
```

The exact slot numbers and assertion reflect this installation; a regression fixture should assert the behavior, not those numbers. No session IDs, task titles, tokens, credentials, or raw feed payload are included here. The user's visual report establishes that two Lines appeared red; database inspection establishes their projected statuses, not a separate physical controller readback.

The current source maps approval attention to `blocked` ([`semantic_status`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/cbb948516eb161d551d817c7ee2870b2b74dc9cb/bridge/shared_input.py#L333-L340)) and retains the old turn/status when a session is stale ([`_project`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/cbb948516eb161d551d817c7ee2870b2b74dc9cb/bridge/shared_input.py#L355-L366)). The installed runtime uses the same relevant rule. This explains the persistent local red projection. It does **not** prove whether the original approvals are still open or identify which upstream observation became ambiguous.

## Scope

Trace the approval lifecycle across the shared state owner/collector and Nanoleaf projection. Determine why these Codex Desktop records retain ambiguous approval attention, and repair the responsible boundary so resolved approvals stop occupying red Lines while genuine approvals remain visible. Preserve the shared owner as the status authority, the single light writer, task allocations and preferences, and the established stale-data safeguards. If the defect is upstream, link and coordinate an owner-repository issue rather than reinterpreting provider events in the Nanoleaf consumer.

This issue is **source-only**. It does not authorize changing the installed runtime, resetting task state, acknowledging notices, or operating the physical lights.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A focused regression scenario reproduces uncertain/stale approval evidence retaining a red assignment after the actual approval has resolved, and distinguishes it from a genuinely pending approval.
- [x] The responsible source or projection is corrected so fresh resolution evidence clears the red status; an unresolved approval stays red. Reconnection, missing events, and uncertainty do not silently claim a resolution.
- [x] Consumer health or diagnostics make a retained uncertain status distinguishable from a confirmed current block, without exposing private session metadata or credentials.
- [x] Existing allocation, pulse/alert priority, shared-source selection, and single-writer behavior remain intact.
- [x] The fix is verified with isolated state and fake transport; any later installation and visible-light acceptance are recorded separately.

## Verification approach

Use a minimal shared snapshot/event sequence with an approval, ambiguous or missing follow-up evidence, and a reliable resolution event. Check the shared owner's semantic state, the Nanoleaf projected status and freshness, and the fake-rendered Line color at each step. Run the repository's Python checks after Python changes. If the map/API changes, run browser checks too. Do not use live credentials or reset the installed database as a test fixture.

## Dependencies and related work

- [Nanoleaf #29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29) delivered the shared consumer; [#30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/30) installed and qualified the basic shared-monitoring path.
- Shared state ownership and provider interpretation belong to [agent-device-hub](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub). The confirmed upstream recovery gap is tracked in [Hub #185](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/185) and delivered in Hub PR #187.
- Delivery target: **source-only**. Source delivery: [Nanoleaf PR #73](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/73), merged as `680acb5c22baafad60f849afd72bcfdabc6bbabf`. Installation remains separate.

Scope: trace the shared approval evidence through the Hub owner and Nanoleaf projection, add focused regression coverage, implement the responsible source fix, and deliver through reviewed PRs with a linked Hub guide synchronization. This is source-only; the installed runtime and lights are outside this delivery.

Upstream recovery is tracked in [Hub #185](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/185). The map API returned HTTP 200. Assigned slots 4 and 13 remain `blocked` with `statusEvidence: uncertain`, as specified until matched evidence or an explicit guarded recovery.

title: Investigate and resolve retained shared unread indicators
body:
## Desired outcome

The wall map's task count reflects current, actionable shared state. Resolved or acknowledged work leaves the indicator set when the shared owner provides reliable evidence; genuinely unread notices and unresolved attention remain visible.

## Evidence and question

Two screenshots on 2026-09-23 showed 71, then 72 tasks in the right column. An aggregate, read-only inspection of the installed Linux state at the second observation found 65 unread, 5 blocked and 2 working sessions, matching the 72 displayed tasks. The shared snapshot had 119 sessions, including 47 idle sessions that the map did not display. This establishes where the count comes from, not whether the 65 unread notices are still actionable. The installed runtime may differ from later source releases.

The map server includes every session in working, question, blocked or unread status. The shared consumer derives unread from owner read and notice evidence. Trace that evidence before changing retention or presentation.

## Scope

Investigate representative unread sessions from source observation through shared owner, Nanoleaf projection and map count using sanitized aggregate evidence. Classify legitimate unread state, unavailable read evidence, delayed or missed transitions, and projection defects. Repair a confirmed defect in its owning repository, or create and link the exact upstream issue if this repository cannot own the fix. Document the supported per-notice recovery path when state is legitimately retained without read evidence.

Do not clear unread by age, truncate the API count, write Codex's private state, bulk-acknowledge notices, or reset the installed database. The approval-specific recovery delivered in [Nanoleaf #72](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/72) and [Hub #185](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/185) is related but does not establish the cause of this unread count.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A sanitized count breakdown reconciles owner sessions and notices, projected statuses, and map tasks for a fixed snapshot. It explains which records should still appear and why.
- [ ] Focused fixtures cover a genuinely unread notice, qualified read evidence, explicit acknowledgment, a new turn under the configured consumer policy, uncertain or unavailable evidence, and restart/reconnect. Counts and Line allocation follow the documented state in each case.
- [ ] Any confirmed lifecycle defect is fixed at the owning boundary and verified without dropping genuine notices. If the observed growth is expected under the available evidence, record that finding and a specific supported cleanup action or separately scoped follow-up rather than claiming a code fix.
- [ ] A corrected indicator leaves the visible task count and waiting allocation without disturbing other tasks, project preferences, modes, scenes or device ownership.

## Verification and delivery

Use isolated shared snapshots and fake device transport. Run `python3 scripts/check.py`; run `npm run test:browser` if the map or API changes. Follow the applicable OpenSpec and workflow checks for a behavior change. Source-only delivery through the repository PR and review gates; installed and physical-light acceptance remain separate. No live task acknowledgment or installation is authorized by this issue.

## Dependencies

No implementation prerequisite. Coordinate owner-side findings with the Hub rather than adding provider event interpretation to the Nanoleaf consumer. Pair the count diagnosis with the task-list presentation issue, which must keep the full count truthful.

title: Show Codex titles and projects for shared tasks, with distinct fallback names
body:
## Problem

In shared mode, the wall names every task `Task shared-<one hex digit>` and shows no project. A read-only snapshot of the installation on 2026-09-23 had 119 shared sessions. None had a hub `label` or `projectId`, and all 72 visible tasks used the fallback name.

There are two causes:

- **The Codex metadata reader is off in shared mode.** `bridge/wall_server.py` skips the reader when shared input is selected, so Codex titles and projects never reach shared tasks. The hub feed carries only user-chosen labels and project IDs, and nothing sets them today.
- **The fallback name is too short to tell tasks apart.** It is `'Task ' + sid[:8]`. Shared keys start with `shared-`, which leaves one hex digit. Legacy keys are Codex UUIDv7 thread IDs, whose first 8 characters encode a timestamp, so tasks started close together collide too. On 2026-09-24, 32 installed sessions had only 29 distinct prefixes.

After the [#89](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/89) rollback on 2026-09-24, legacy mode shows titles and projects again because the reader is on. This issue brings the same data to shared mode.

## Outcome

Shared Codex tasks show the same titles and projects as legacy mode. Tasks without a title, such as Claude Code tasks or Codex tasks missing from the index, get a distinct, readable fallback name.

## Scope

This is a personal installation: Codex, the hub and the wall run on one host. That keeps the change small.

- **Look up Codex sessions locally.** In shared mode, keep the existing metadata reader running. For sessions whose `identity.provider` is `codex`, look up `identity.sessionId` in the configured Codex files. Apply the same title and project rules as legacy mode.
- **Do the lookup in the shared projection.** Put it in `shared_input._project`, not in the map server. The project drives Line allocation, and `_project` rewrites `task_info` on every poll.
- **Enrich only sessions in the current feed.** A lookup never creates, restores or renews a task. Retirement under [Hub #195](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/195) stays authoritative.
- **Use one precedence order.** A manual project override wins. Next comes a hub label or `projectId`, then Codex metadata. Without any of these, the task gets the fallback name and no project.
- **Build the fallback from the end of the ID.** Use the provider plus the last 8 hex characters of `identity.sessionId`, for example `Codex 5b1e07c2` or `Claude 4227761b`. Use the end because the start of a UUIDv7 is a timestamp. Legacy mode uses the same rule.
- **Document it briefly.** Add a short paragraph on precedence and the fallback name to `bridge/README.md`.

What stays the same:

- The map reads Codex files and never writes them.
- Nothing new is uploaded to the hub feed.
- The hub and its contracts do not change.

Out of scope:

- **Claude Code titles and projects from local Claude Code data.** Tracked in [#100](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/100). Until then, these tasks use the fallback name or a label set in the hub dashboard.
- **Host and source identity checks beyond the provider.** Codex thread IDs are UUIDs, so provider plus session ID is enough on one machine.
- **A provenance document, source-qualification rules and an upstream owner issue.**

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] In shared mode, a Codex session whose thread ID appears in the configured Codex files shows that title and project. Line allocation uses that project.
- [x] A Claude Code session with the same raw session ID as a Codex thread does not receive the Codex title or project.
- [x] A hub label or `projectId` wins over Codex metadata. A manual project override wins over both and survives restarts and legacy/shared switching.
- [x] Tasks without a title show the provider plus the last 8 hex characters of their session ID. Two Codex tasks started seconds apart have distinct names. No `Task shared-*` names remain.
- [x] A session that has left the feed is not recreated or renewed by the lookup.
- [x] Legacy mode behaves as before, apart from the new fallback name.
- [x] `bridge/README.md` documents the precedence order and the fallback name.

## Dependencies

- **Builds on the shared consumer.** That consumer came from [#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29).
- **No hub changes are needed.**
- **Deliver this before [#89](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/89).** That issue removes the legacy hooks, and delivering this first keeps titles and projects through that cutover.

## Verification and delivery

- **Update the spec.** This needs an OpenSpec delta to `shared-session-consumer`, whose "Multiple identities" scenario currently allows only explicit bindings to connect sessions to local presentation data.
- **Test with synthetic sessions.** Cover these cases:
  - a Codex session present in the title index and project assignments
  - a Codex session missing from both
  - a Claude Code session that shares a raw session ID with a Codex thread
  - a hub label
  - a manual override
  - two Codex UUIDv7 IDs a few seconds apart
  - switching between legacy and shared mode
- **Run the checks.** Run `python3 scripts/check.py`, `npm run test:browser`, and the OpenSpec workflow checks.
- **Get human approval.** The fallback name is a UI change.
- **Deliver as source only.** Ship through one reviewed PR. Installation is separate.

title: Queue the completion comet when a subagent delays a parent's unread
body:
## Problem

After [#74](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/74) ([PR #80](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/80)), subagent sessions count as part of their parent task. A parent's completion can then skip its celebration comet. This happens when the parent's turn ends while the owner still counts a subagent active.

When the parent's turn-ended notice first appears, the task still shows working because of that subagent, so no comet is queued. When the subagent later finishes or goes silent, the task becomes unread. By then the notice was already present in the prior snapshot, and the consumer queues comets only for notices that are new relative to the prior snapshot. The unread color and its outward wave still show; only the one-time comet is lost. This was found in PR #80's round-5 Standards review, finding S12.

## Desired outcome

A top-level completion notice queues one completion comet the first time its task becomes visibly unread, even when a subagent delayed that transition. A notice that was already celebrated is never celebrated again. That includes a task that returns to unread after a subagent's later work.

## Scope and acceptance criteria

- [ ] The parent's notice arrives while a subagent is counted active. The subagent then finishes or goes silent, and exactly one comet is queued in Work.
- [ ] A notice that was already celebrated while its task was unread is not celebrated again when a later subagent run ends.
- [ ] Interruption, resync, stale evidence and Free/Quiet keep their existing comet rules. Started comet reservations are unaffected.
- [ ] Any retained celebration state is private and survives restart without replaying old comets. Legacy mode is unchanged.

## Verification

Add focused `tests/test_shared_input.py` cases using the fake clock and isolated state, and run `python3 scripts/check.py`. If behavior changes, update the `shared-session-consumer` spec through an OpenSpec change.

## Dependencies

Requires #74 / PR #80 to be merged. This is source-only work; it needs no installation or device checks.

## Work assessment

- **Complexity: medium.** Comparison against the prior snapshot plus subagent-active counting.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Root cause diagnosed in the PR #80 review.
- **Impact: low.** A missed celebration is cosmetic.

title: Remove the legacy Codex hooks after the shared-input cutover
body:
## Outcome

With shared input selected, Codex no longer runs the legacy `bridge.py hook` on every event. One command removes those hooks, and one command restores them for a rollback to legacy input.

## Why

The legacy hook is still registered for seven events in both Codex homes, including PreToolUse and PostToolUse, so it runs twice per tool call. In shared mode, `handle_event` reads `config.json`, opens `status.sqlite`, takes its write lock twice and returns without doing anything else. Each run costs about 50 ms of Python startup and imports. Codex waits for these hooks. If one arrives while the worker holds the write lock during a device write, it can wait up to 2.5 s before failing open.

The hub's shared hook covers the events that shared mode uses, and it doesn't register PreToolUse or PostToolUse. Removing the legacy hooks loses only the rollback path. `shared-select legacy` depends on legacy hook events to clear restored steady colors and to create new tasks.

There is no supported way to remove only these hooks. `setup --uninstall` removes them but also switches every device to Free. Running a fresh `setup` to add them back clears task records.

## Scope

- [x] `hooks remove` deletes only the entries tagged `nanoleaf-codex-status-v1` from a Codex home's `hooks.json`. Every other entry, including the hub's shared hook, stays byte for byte. It keeps a private backup outside Git and changes no mode, task or device state.
