title: Wake the worker from the hub's change stream instead of polling each second
body:
## Outcome

The wall reacts to a new hub revision as soon as the hub announces it, instead of on the worker's next 1-second poll.

## Current behavior

In shared mode, `Poller.tick` fetches `GET /api/monitor/v1/sessions` at the start of each worker pass, at most once a second. Between passes the worker sleeps in 0.25 s steps and wakes early only for local changes (`event_revision` or a preview). A hub revision reaches `PUT /effects` about 0 to 1.3 s later, plus device round trips.

The hub also serves `GET /api/monitor/v1/changes`, a Server-Sent Events stream that announces a new revision without carrying session data. Nanoleaf doesn't use it. The hub currently checks for changes on a 1-second timer, so listening won't help until [agent-device-hub#222](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/222) makes it push on commit.

## Scope

- [ ] A listener thread in the shared-input worker keeps `/changes` open with the existing read token and endpoint checks (numeric loopback only, owner-only token file). It sends `Last-Event-ID` when it reconnects.
- [ ] A `state` or `resync` event wakes the worker, which fetches `/sessions` at once through the existing poller. The snapshot stays the only source of session state.
- [ ] The worker's sleep ends on that signal as well as on local changes.
- [ ] Polling stays as the fallback. While the stream is healthy the poll can slow down, for example to 5 s. When the stream is down it returns to 1 s. Choose the values during delivery.
- [ ] The listener is bounded: a connect deadline, a reconnect when heartbeats stop for a few seconds, backoff and no unbounded buffering. A stream failure alone never marks sessions stale; staleness still comes only from failed snapshot fetches.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests with a fake hub stream cover:
  - an event that triggers an immediate fetch
  - `resync`
  - reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID`
  - a stream that goes silent
  - the stream being down while polling still works
- [ ] An event with no snapshot change sends nothing to the panels.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` passes, and an OpenSpec change updates the `shared-session-consumer` spec.
- [ ] Live, when the owner explicitly requests the installed update and hub #222 is installed: submit a Codex prompt and confirm the wall reacts. One comment records it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by [agent-device-hub#222](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/222).

## Not included

Tidbyt, the hub dashboard and any change to the session snapshot format.

## Readiness

Complexity small to medium. Uncertainty low. Backlog until hub #222 merges. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

## Work assessment

title: Let Codex play saved Nanoleaf scenes through the local MCP server
body:
## Outcome

You can ask Codex to play a scene you saved in the Nanoleaf app, for example "switch the wall to Free and play Aurora", through the local MCP server.

## Current behavior

The controller already supports `scene.activate` for discovered scenes, in Free mode only (#64). The local MCP server exposes only `nanoleaf_status` and `nanoleaf_mode_set`, and the `local-mcp-bindings` spec forbids scene tools. Scene IDs are opaque. The names you chose in the Nanoleaf app travel in the `nanoleaf.integration/1.0` snapshot. Codex isn't configured to use the MCP server yet.

## Scope

- [ ] A read tool lists the advertised scenes with their IDs and names.
- [ ] A control tool, `nanoleaf_scene_activate`, sends one `scene.activate` through the controller. Like `nanoleaf_mode_set`, it passes the caller's request ID and expected revisions through unchanged.
- [ ] Following hub ADR 0005, activation stays a separate command. The tool doesn't switch to Free itself. In Work or Quiet it returns the controller's rejection with a message to switch to Free first.
- [ ] An unknown scene ID is rejected before dispatch. The tools appear only for credentials with the matching read or control scope.
- [ ] An OpenSpec change updates the `local-mcp-bindings` spec, and `docs/local-mcp.md` describes the tools.

title: Play custom animations on the Lines when Codex asks for them
body:
## Outcome

You can describe an animation to Codex, such as "a slow blue-green ocean wave". Codex switches the wall to Free and plays it on the Lines through the local MCP server.

## Background

A custom Nanoleaf animation is a `display` effect: frames for each panel, uploaded once with `PUT /effects` and then looped by the device. The worker already builds and uploads this kind of effect for status (`effect_payload` in `bridge/bridge.py`). A requested animation reuses the same path and the same single writer, with no per-frame streaming.

Nothing accepts animation input today. Controller v1 has no animation command. The hub architecture requires typed-extension work for arbitrary color or timeline input and rules out raw protocol commands.

## Decision

The owner chose Free-mode content on September 23, 2026. When you ask for an animation in conversation, the agent switches the wall to Free with `nanoleaf_mode_set`, then plays the animation. It stays until the next mode command, animation or scene. This fits hub [ADR 0005](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md) as written: switching to Free is its own command, and nothing restores automatically.

Animations that play over Work status to get your attention are wanted too, but as scheduled or routine behavior, not on request. They are out of scope here (see Not included).

## Scope

- [ ] A typed `animation.play` command in the Nanoleaf extension, not a controller v1 change. Parameters: a pattern from a fixed set (for example wave, pulse, breathe, sparkle and gradient), 1 to 8 `#rrggbb` colors, speed, direction for spatial patterns, and whether it loops or plays once. The controller validates everything before queueing.
- [ ] The worker separates the frame encoder from the status color logic, and renders each pattern with the Lines geometry it already uses for waves and comets.
- [ ] Commands use the existing queue and receipts: sent, failed or uncertain, with physical outcome unknown. Like `scene.activate`, the command is accepted only in Free. In Work or Quiet the controller rejects it before any write, and the MCP tool's message says to switch to Free first.
- [ ] The local MCP server gets a read tool that lists patterns and limits, and a control tool, `nanoleaf_animation_play`.
- [ ] Qualify the firmware's limits on effect size and frame count, and keep requests within the controller's 64 KiB limit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover validation bounds, encoder output for each pattern on fixture layouts, acceptance in Free and rejection in Work and Quiet, receipts and the MCP tools.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` and `npm run test:mcp` pass. OpenSpec changes update the affected controller, worker and MCP specs.
- [ ] Live, when the owner explicitly requests it: ask Codex for two different animations, and confirm it switches the wall to Free before each one plays. One comment records it.

## Related

- #91 lets Codex play saved scenes and sets up the same MCP connection.
- #19 and #20 (status animation presets) could reuse the new encoder.
- #15 (authoritative rendering state).
- [agent-device-hub#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/41) needs real-time streaming for music visualizers. This issue doesn't.

## Not included

Per-panel keyframes, the NL22 Panels, audio-reactive or streamed effects, and the hub's MCP route. Also attention animations over Work status: they belong with scheduled or routine behavior under [agent-device-hub#45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45), and playing over status will need its own ADR 0005 decision. They can reuse this issue's encoder. Also ChatGPT and other remote clients: ChatGPT connects to MCP servers only over remote HTTPS, which depends on the remote access that hub ADR 0004 defers.

## Readiness

Complexity medium. Uncertainty low; the firmware limits are the main unknown. No blockers. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Show Claude Code titles and projects for shared tasks
body:
## Problem

After [#75](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/75), shared Codex tasks get titles and projects from Codex's local files. Claude Code tasks still show only the fallback name, such as `Claude 4227761b`, and no project, unless someone sets a label in the hub dashboard. The hub feed does not carry Claude Code titles or working folders, by design.

## Evidence

A read-only check on 2026-09-24 found:

- **The session ID matches the transcript name.** The hub uses the Claude Code hook's `session_id` as `identity.sessionId` (`packages/agent-state/src/providers.ts` in agent-device-hub). Claude Code stores each session at `~/.claude/projects/<encoded folder>/<session_id>.jsonl`. All 1,606 `custom-title` entries in the 40 most recent WSL transcripts carried the same `sessionId` as their file name.
- **Most sessions have a title.** 33 of those 40 transcripts contain a `custom-title` entry, whose `customTitle` field holds the title. The entry repeats, so the last one is current.
- **Sessions record their folder.** `user` entries carry `cwd`. 27 of the 40 transcripts used one `cwd`. The rest changed folder during the session, for example into a worktree.
- **Codex project roots already match WSL paths.** 30 of 31 Codex project roots are `\\wsl.localhost\...` paths. The existing `normalize` in `bridge/project_map.py` converts these to Linux paths, so the legacy root-prefix rule can match a Claude Code `cwd` to a Codex project.
- **There are two Claude Code homes.** WSL has `~/.claude`, and Windows has `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`. It is not yet known which one feeds the hub.

## Outcome

Shared Claude Code tasks show their Claude Code title. When a task's working folder is inside a Codex project root, the task also shows that project.

## Scope

- **Look up Claude Code sessions locally.** For sessions whose `identity.provider` is `claude`, read the transcript named `identity.sessionId` in the configured Claude Code home. Do this in `shared_input._project`, alongside the #75 lookup.
- **Title:** use the latest `customTitle` in the transcript.
- **Project:** match the session's `cwd` against Codex project roots with the existing `normalize` and root-prefix rule. A folder outside every root gets no project.
- **Precedence:** keep the #75 order. A manual override wins, then a hub label or `projectId`, then local metadata, then the fallback name.
- **Read incrementally.** Transcripts are large and grow while a session runs. Cache per file by size and modification time, and read only new bytes or the tail. Never parse a whole transcript on every poll.
- **Tolerate format changes.** The transcript format is internal to Claude Code and undocumented. A missing file, unreadable line or unknown shape leaves the fallback name and no project, and the projection still succeeds.
- **Read only what is needed.** Take `custom-title` and `cwd` only. Never read prompt or message content into the wall's state, logs or browser responses.

What stays the same:

- The map never writes Claude Code files.
- Nothing new is uploaded to the hub feed.

## Decisions to settle before ready

- **Which Claude Code home to read:** WSL, Windows, or both. Also the configuration keys that name them.
- **Which `cwd` to use when a session changes folder:** the first, the latest, or the most frequent.
- **What to show when there is no `custom-title`:** keep the fallback name, or derive a title such as the folder name.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A shared Claude Code session whose transcript has a `custom-title` shows the latest title.
- [ ] A Claude Code session whose `cwd` is inside a Codex project root shows that project, and Line allocation uses it. Other sessions have no project.
- [ ] A Codex session with the same raw session ID as a Claude Code transcript does not receive the Claude Code title or project.
- [ ] Hub labels, hub `projectId` values and manual overrides keep the #75 precedence.
- [ ] A missing, unreadable or unrecognized transcript leaves the fallback name and no project, and the projection still succeeds.
- [ ] Polling cost stays bounded as transcripts grow.
- [ ] Prompt and message content may appear once jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#425 lands. Credentials and tokens never appear in the wall's state, logs or browser responses.
- [ ] `bridge/README.md` documents the Claude Code source and its limits.

## Dependencies

- [#75](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/75): the shared-mode lookup, precedence order and fallback name.
- The decisions listed above.

## Verification and delivery

- **Update the spec.** Extend the #75 OpenSpec delta to Claude Code.
- **Test with synthetic transcripts.** Cover these cases:
  - with and without a `custom-title`
  - several `custom-title` entries
  - a folder change during the session
  - a `cwd` inside and outside a Codex project root
  - a large file that grows between polls
  - a malformed line
  - a Codex session that shares the raw session ID
- **Run the checks.** Run `python3 scripts/check.py`, `npm run test:browser`, and the OpenSpec workflow checks.
- **Deliver as source only.** Ship through one reviewed PR. Installation is separate.

**Policy update (2026-09-25):** the owner retired the rule that kept titles, project names, prompts, transcripts and paths out of shared data (jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#424). Credentials and tokens stay excluded. This story's text was updated to match. The hub now plans to supply Claude Code and Codex titles and project names to every device (jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#424). Coordinate with #179, so the wall reads them from the hub instead of maintaining its own Claude Code reader, or keeps its reader only as a fallback.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** The three decisions the story says to settle before ready: which Claude Code homes to read, which working directory to use after a folder change, and the fallback title. Also reconcile the tracked blocker (#111) with the body's #75.

**Reassess when:** Those decisions are recorded.
**Assessed:** 2026-09-25 · policy `agent-skills@3746fab` · evidence: story text, comments and dependencies read 2026-09-25 03:10 UTC; no ratings recorded; re-confirmed 2026-09-25 after the owner's data-policy update, ratings unchanged · fingerprint: `2b49f5a0c7ce`

**Note:** Show Claude Code titles and projects for shared tasks, as [[N75]] does for Codex. The hub feed deliberately carries neither, so the wall reads them locally by session ID. Waits for [[N111]] and three owner decisions.
**Highlight:** decision, Choose which Claude Code home to read, which working folder counts when a session moves, and the fallback when a session has no title.

title: Open a wall task's thread in Codex Desktop
body:
## Problem

The wall map shows each task's title, project and status, but gives no way to get from a task to its conversation. To continue a task, the user has to find the thread in Codex Desktop by name.

## Evidence

A read-only check on 2026-09-24 found:

- **Codex Desktop opens thread links.** The installed app (`OpenAI.Codex_26.917.9434.0`, MSIX) registers the `codex://` scheme on Windows. Its deep-link parser maps `codex://threads/<threadId>` to a local conversation and accepts an optional `hostId`. Codex's own "Copy deep link" action produces the same form. The format is internal and undocumented, so a later Codex release could change it.
- **Legacy task IDs are Desktop thread UUIDs.** The unread reader compares Desktop thread IDs directly against `sessions.id` (`bridge/bridge.py:281-283`), and `/api/state` already sends that ID to the browser.
- **Shared task IDs are hashes.** The key is `'shared-' + sha256(identity)` (`bridge/shared_input.py:31`, `:59-60`). The raw `identity.provider`, `client` and `sessionId` survive only in the stored envelope (`bridge/shared_input.py:207`, `:479`). Subagents fold into their top-level ancestor (`bridge/shared_input.py:362-379`).
- **Desktop can open only its own threads.** Codex Desktop and the WSL CLI keep separate homes. The Desktop index (`%USERPROFILE%\.codex\session_index.jsonl`) had 295 threads and the WSL index 33, with none in common.
- **The link is clicked on the same machine.** The map is opened in the Windows browser at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`, next to Codex Desktop. The map's CSP (`bridge/wall_server.py:147-152`) sets no navigation restriction, so a top-level link to `codex://` should not be blocked. The browser asks "Open Codex?" the first time and offers "Always allow".

## Desired outcome

The inspector's task detail card shows an "Open in Codex" link for Codex Desktop tasks. Clicking it opens that thread in Codex Desktop.

## Scope

- **Expose the link from the server.** `/api/state` adds `codexUrl` to a task only when it is a Desktop thread:
  - Legacy: the task ID is a UUID present in the configured Desktop title index.
  - Shared: the presented root session has `identity.provider` `codex`, `identity.client` `desktop` and a UUID `sessionId`.
- **Build the URL safely.** The server validates the UUID and builds `codex://threads/<uuid>`. The browser never builds the URL from free text.
- **Render a real link.** Put a labelled, keyboard-reachable `<a href>` without `target` in the task detail card built by `inspect()` (`bridge/wall.html:856-886`). Add `codexUrl` to the card's fingerprint (`bridge/wall.html:868`) so the card refreshes when the link appears or changes.
- **Show nothing for other tasks.** Codex CLI, Claude Code, non-UUID and unknown tasks get no link.
- **Correct the footer.** It says "Opening a task here does not mark it read" (`bridge/wall.html:398`). Selecting a task in the map still does not mark it read. Opening it in Codex lets Codex mark it read, and the bridge follows through the existing unread reader.
- **Document it.** Describe the link, which tasks get it and the read behavior in `bridge/README.md`.

What stays the same:

- Clicking the link sends no request to the map server. The map writes no Codex data and marks nothing read.
- The controller and integration APIs do not gain the URL.
- The hub and its contracts do not change.

Out of scope:

- **Links in task rows.** Keeps the reduced controls planned in #78.
- **Claude Code sessions.** No deep link was investigated. Track separately if wanted.
- **Codex CLI threads and remote `hostId` hosts.**
- **Lively and the inspection-only display mode** (#12, #14).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A legacy task whose thread is in the Desktop index shows "Open in Codex" with href `codex://threads/<id>`. Clicking it in the Windows browser opens that thread in Codex Desktop.
- [x] A shared Codex Desktop task shows the link for its root session. A subagent task folded into its parent links to the parent's thread.
- [x] Codex CLI tasks, Claude Code tasks and tasks with a non-UUID or unknown ID show no link.
- [x] Clicking the link issues no request to the map server, and no write, unread acknowledgment, Locate or device request.
- [x] Unread state clears only through the existing unread reader after Codex marks the thread read.
- [x] The link is keyboard reachable, has an accessible label, and fits narrow layouts without horizontal overflow.
- [x] `bridge/README.md` documents the link, its eligibility rule and the read behavior.

## Verification approach

- **Update the spec.** Add an OpenSpec delta to `wall-task-inspector`, and to `shared-session-consumer` for exposing a link derived from the shared identity.
- **Python tests** for `codexUrl`: a legacy thread in the index, a legacy thread missing from it, a shared Desktop session, a shared CLI session, a Claude Code session, a folded subagent and a malformed ID.
- **Browser test** (`npm run test:browser`): the link's href and label, keyboard access, a narrow viewport, the updated footer, and no non-GET request when the link is activated.
- **Run the checks.** `python3 scripts/check.py`, `npm run test:browser` and the OpenSpec workflow checks.
- **Manual Windows check.** Open one real Desktop thread from the map in the Windows browser. Report it separately from installation and physical-light checks, which this issue does not need.
- **Get human approval.** This is a UI change.

## Dependencies

- **Land after #75.** It changes how shared sessions' `identity` reaches the projection, which this issue also reads.
- **Land after #105.** It changes inspector selection, in the same code as the detail card.
- **Shared assumption with #75:** for Codex Desktop sessions, the hub's `identity.sessionId` is the Desktop thread UUID.

## Delivery target

Source-only.

title: Switch Nanoleaf between Work and Free based on monitored session presence
body:
## Desired outcome

For an explicitly enabled Nanoleaf device, enter native Work mode while the selected shared owner has monitored sessions, and enter native Free mode when the last session ends or expires.

User-approved behavior, September 24, 2026:

- Waiting, completed and read-but-still-tracked sessions keep Work enabled between prompts.
- Free uses the existing native scene/app handoff.
- A manual Work/Quiet/Free selection pauses automation until explicit re-enable, including across restart.
- Automation is Nanoleaf-only and disabled by default.

This changes the selected mode. Existing Work-mode idle scene restoration alone does not provide that mode switch.

## Bounded implementation

Use the existing Nanoleaf worker, feed reads and guarded native mode operation. No new daemon, scheduler, rules engine, provider hook, dashboard or restoration-history service.

### One persistent setting

Use one automation-enabled boolean per participating registered device:

- Explicit enable sets it to true and reconciles current session presence.
- Explicit disable sets it to false without an extra mode command.
- A user mode command sets it to false, including selection of the already-current mode. Automatic commands do not disable themselves.
- Persist the flag. A separate paused state, resume-cycle counter, reason history or saved pre-Work mode is unnecessary.
- Provide local enable, disable and status controls. Do not discover or enroll devices automatically.

Apply manual precedence through the existing shared mode operation used by the CLI, wall map, tray and controller API. Preserve its guards so pending automatic decisions cannot override a newer manual selection.

### One presence rule

When enabled and the feed is valid with a running owner:

| Owner snapshot | Desired native mode |
| --- | --- |
| One or more session records | Work |
| No session records | Free |
| Feed missing, invalid, disconnected or owner not running | Hold current mode |

Count all session records in the selected feed, including children and all supported provider/client paths. Do not count only `activity: active`, visible rows or allocated Lines. The shared owner decides retirement; Nanoleaf adds no provider interpretation.

Reconcile on presence changes, explicit enable, startup and recovery using the current snapshot. Skip a command when the desired mode is already selected. Additional starts/ends while presence remains nonzero cause no mode write. Repeated polls and duplicate snapshots do not repeatedly command devices; do not replay missed transitions. A retire/resume interval unseen between reads need not cause a pointless Free/Work cycle.

Retain existing bounded controller failure handling and receipts. Yield on observed external control or conflicts rather than repeatedly taking over; do not add vendor-app detection. Keep one writer per device and independent failures. Preserve native power-off behavior, Work/Free scene and brightness policies, reservations and task/effect state. Add no power/brightness commands, selected-scene override or old-effect replay.

This explicitly enabled automation is a narrow exception to manual-only mode selection. Update the owning mode/shared-input specification and guide during implementation; leave other device families and hub preset policy unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disabled automation sends no mode commands. Enable/disable/status reflect the persisted flag.
- [ ] First session presence requests Work once; the last record's removal requests Free once. Multiple sessions and child records keep presence nonzero.
- [ ] Mixed-provider snapshots from the owner implementing [Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241) cover Codex Desktop, Codex CLI and Claude Code. Removing the last record after any supported provider's accepted session end requests Free without waiting for the 24-hour fallback; another remaining record keeps Work enabled. Nanoleaf does not interpret hooks or hide retained records to compensate for an older owner policy.
- [ ] Ordinary completion, waiting, read/acknowledgment changes, five-minute freshness uncertainty and turns exceeding 30 minutes do not cause Free. Owner retirement/expiry does.
- [ ] Every existing explicit mode-command entry point disables automation, even for the current mode. The flag survives restart/reconnect; only explicit re-enable resumes automation.
- [ ] Invalid/unavailable feeds hold the current mode. Startup, recovery and enable reconcile a current valid snapshot without historical replay.
- [ ] Duplicate snapshots, quick end/resume, repeated polls and concurrent manual selection cause no redundant mode writes or manual override reversal.
- [ ] Focused fake-device checks preserve native Free handoff, power-off, scenes/brightness, reservations and no-old-effect-replay behavior. Failures and uncertain outcomes remain bounded and do not affect other devices.

## Verification approach

Extend existing isolated-state, fake-clock, shared-feed and fake-device tests for the scenarios above. Reuse existing mode/queue coverage rather than duplicate controller suites. Add issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts and affected guide/development updates, and run applicable repository checks. There is no new UI scope.

Installation and visible-light verification remain separate, requiring a named owner, explicit target and authorized sequence. Observe first-session Work, last-session Free, a long turn, manual disable and restart/reconnect behavior. Source or transport success is not physical acceptance.

## Dependencies and delivery target

- **Blocked by [Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241)**, which applies the same owner rule to Codex CLI and Claude Code. **Satisfied prerequisite: [Hub #218](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/218)** delivered retirement and fresh-record reconciliation; its closed native link remains provenance. Next action: deliver the consistent owner policy, then validate this consumer against that compatible owner release. Session retention is decided by the owner; ordinary completion/waiting remains tracked, and absent/lost ends still use the existing evidence expiry.
- Existing prerequisites are complete: [shared sessions #29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29), [per-device workers #42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/42) and [native controls #64](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/64).
- [Hub #67](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67) owns explicit multi-device presets; [Hub #45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45) owns broader automation. Neither is a prerequisite.

Source-only; backlog/blocked only on the unfinished Hub #241 prerequisite. Scope simplified with the user on September 24, 2026; the subsequent planning update requires consistent owner retirement across supported providers. The agreed presence rule, manual override and Nanoleaf-only scope remain. This tracker revision authorizes no implementation, installation, personal settings change or physical device operation.

## Planning assessment and qualification boundary

Refreshed September 25, 2026. #218's accepted-end source/installed archive scope is complete. [Hub #253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253) owns native Desktop idle/shutdown, reopen-without-prompt and live-resume qualification; this automation promises a response to authoritative owner presence, not reliable native end emission on quit or after thirty minutes. Existing source scope and physical-acceptance boundaries are unchanged.

Device-only Evict leaves the owner record present and must keep Work selected while automation is enabled. The planned [shared-owner Evict everywhere (Hub #262)](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/262) removes presence; after the last record is removed, normal reconciliation selects Free. This adds no separate mode command to eviction and no new prerequisite for #110. Add the corresponding synthetic presence examples when the shared command is available; current first/last presence tests already define the mode rule.

Complexity medium: worker reconciliation, persistent enable flag and manual-mode entry points. Uncertainty medium: supported owner policy awaits #241 and integration needs focused fake-device evidence. Impact medium: automatic mode changes can disrupt the user's selected output, protected by explicit opt-in, one writer and persistent manual precedence. Remains blocked on #241; do not mark ready merely because #218 completed.

title: Keep following the hub feed when it contains an undeclared source
body:
## Problem

Nanoleaf rejects the whole hub snapshot when any session comes from a source that isn't in `qualifiedSources`. `check_envelope` in `bridge/shared_input.py` raises `unqualified-source`. The feed then counts as failed: tasks are marked stale, colors hold and the wall stops following every agent, not just the new one. It stays that way until someone edits the consumer configuration.

The installed configuration declares only Codex Desktop and Codex CLI. The hub has no Claude Code sessions today, but the first Claude Code hook that posts to it would stop the wall. #100 expects Claude Code tasks on the wall.

## Outcome

A session from a source Nanoleaf hasn't declared stays off the wall, and every other session keeps updating. Once you declare a Claude Code source, its sessions appear.

## Scope

- [ ] Skip sessions from undeclared sources instead of rejecting the snapshot. A skipped session gets no slot, wave, comet or acknowledgment, and takes no part in parent and subagent grouping.
- [ ] Envelope checks still reject the whole snapshot: authentication, version, owner, schema and revision.
- [ ] `shared-status` reports how many sessions were skipped and their source identities, so a missing declaration is visible.
- [ ] Declaring a source later with `shared-configure` doesn't replay old comets or waves for its existing sessions.
- [ ] Test that `qualifiedSources` accepts a Claude Code source identity. Update `docs/shared-input.md`, which says every source in the feed must be declared, and describe how to declare one.
- [ ] An OpenSpec change updates the `shared-session-consumer` spec.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover:
  - one undeclared session among declared ones
  - a snapshot with only undeclared sessions, which leaves the wall idle and the connection current
  - a declared Claude Code source
  - declaring a source after its sessions already exist
  - a declared subagent whose parent is undeclared, which follows the existing missing-parent rule
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` passes.

title: Show when the Lines are on hold and how to resume them
body:
## Problem

After a device write with an uncertain result, or a controller command that stays queued for more than 30 s, the worker puts the Lines on hold (`controller_hold_revision`). It stops writing to them so it never repeats a write that may already have landed. To you, the wall just looks frozen on its last display.

Nothing says why. The controller snapshot reports the failed or uncertain `lastOutcome` but not the hold, and the wall map doesn't show it.

Any mode command clears the hold, even one that selects the mode already active. That works from the wall map, CLI, controller or MCP. Power and brightness commands through the controller clear it too.

## Outcome

When the Lines are on hold, the wall map says so, explains why and offers one action to resume.

## Scope

- [ ] The wall map shows the hold, when it started and its cause (an uncertain write or an expired command), with a Resume action that selects the current mode again.
- [ ] The message explains that the worker paused so it wouldn't repeat a write that may have landed.
- [ ] The CLI's status output reports the hold the same way.
- [ ] Resume uses the existing mode path. Nothing retries automatically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover a hold from an uncertain write, a hold from an expired command, Resume clearing it, and no hold shown after a mode, power or brightness command.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` and `npm run test:browser` pass. The PR includes a wall map screenshot in the held state.

## Not included

Showing the hold in the hub dashboard. That needs the `nanoleaf.integration` snapshot to carry it, which changes a schema the hub validates, so it is a separate change in both repositories.

title: Control the NL22 Panels through the controller and local MCP server
body:
## Problem

The protected controller and the local MCP server reach only the Lines (`wall`). The controller has one device identity. Under ADR 0010, only the `wall` worker runs controller and integration work, including overrides, the hold and scene discovery. The NL22 Panels can be controlled only from the CLI (`mode … --device panels`).

So the hub, the dashboard and Codex can't turn the Panels on or off, set their brightness or mode, or play their scenes. #91 and #92 cover the Lines only.

## Outcome

The Panels are a second controller device. The hub, the dashboard and Codex (through MCP) control them the same way as the Lines, and each device keeps its own single writer.

## Scope

- [ ] `/controller/v1/devices` lists both devices. The snapshot, commands, feed and integration routes accept the Panels' `deviceId`, with their own identity, revisions, request journal, overrides, hold and discovered scenes.
- [ ] The Panels worker runs the Panels' controller work and stays the only writer to the Panels. The `wall` worker never writes to them. Update ADR 0010, which assigns all controller work to `wall`.
- [ ] Power, brightness, mode and `scene.activate` work for the Panels under the same mode rules as the Lines.
- [ ] The local MCP server can bind the Panels as a second fixed target. Callers can't choose other devices.
- [ ] Record whether the Panels accept `display` version 2.0 effects, which ADR 0010 lists as unknown. #92 needs that answer before animations can extend to the Panels.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests with fake devices cover both devices side by side:
  - a command for one device never runs on the other's worker
  - a hold on one device doesn't affect the other
  - each device keeps its own revisions and scenes
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` and `npm run test:mcp` pass. OpenSpec changes update the affected controller, worker and MCP specs.
- [ ] Live, when the owner explicitly requests it: add a hub controller entry for the Panels, then change their mode and brightness from the dashboard or Codex. One comment records it.

## Related

- #91 and #92 add scenes and animations for the Lines. Both can extend to the Panels after this.
- #44 and #47 cover the wall map and a combined layout.

## Readiness

title: Change a registered Nanoleaf device's address without re-enrolling
body:
## Desired outcome

Let the operator change the address of a registered Nanoleaf device, such as the NL22 Light Panels after a new DHCP lease, without removing and re-enrolling it. The device keeps its id, reservations, mode, layout and saved scene.

This is a personal project with one operator and one Linux installation. The issue is sized for that.

## Background

`device-enroll` ([#45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/45), PR #79) refuses an existing id at a new address, so it never silently redirects an identity. The only way to change a Panels address today is `device-remove` followed by `device-enroll`, which clears the device's reservations. The [device-state specification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/openspec/specs/device-state/spec.md) already says a configured address change keeps a device's identity and saved state. The Linux guide documents the current workaround.

## Scope

An explicit command or option that changes one registered device's address. Before writing, it verifies the device at the new address with the stored credential, the same way enrollment does: model NL22 and a layout whose triangles match the saved geometry. The Lines device (`wall`) may be covered if that is simple; otherwise it is out of scope.

Out of scope: automatic discovery or following the device on the network, and changing a device's kind.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The operator can change a registered Panels device's address. Its id, reservations, mode, layout and saved scene are unchanged, and it is never registered twice.
- [ ] AC2: Before any write, the new address is checked: it must be a private IPv4 address, unused by another registered device, and answering as the same kind of device with a layout matching the saved one. A mismatch is refused with nothing changed.
- [ ] AC3: The change sends no light write. A running worker for the device picks up the new address on its next pass or retry, without a service restart.
- [ ] AC4: Credentials stay out of output and errors, as with enrollment.
- [ ] AC5: The Linux installation guide replaces the remove-and-re-enroll workaround with the new command.

## Verification approach

Isolated Linux state with fake Lines and NL22 transports. Cover a successful change, a conflicting address, a device that does not match, an unreachable address, and a worker picking up the new address. Run the Python and workflow suites.

## Dependencies

- Builds on #45 (delivered). Not needed for #46 unless the Panels' address changes during that trial.

## Delivery target

Source only. Changing the installed runtime's device address is a separate operator action.

title: Keep completion comets and waves when the worker skips owner revisions
body:
## Problem

In shared mode, the Nanoleaf worker treats any skipped owner revision as a resync (`bridge/shared_input.py`, `_project`: `snapshot['revision'] > previous['snapshot']['revision'] + 1`). A resync:

- sets `shared_wave_cutoff`, so outward waves from earlier epochs are suppressed, and any new or changed status gets an expired epoch;
- deletes every task's comets, including celebrations that are already running;
- skips the unread-comet check, because that check sits in an `elif` after the resync branch.

The worker polls the owner at most once a second, and the Hub commits a revision for every accepted hook event. Two commits between polls are therefore routine: a parent's Stop plus a SubagentStop, or events from another session. When that happens, a new completion gets neither its comet nor its wave, and any running comet stops early.

A skipped revision loses no state. Every snapshot is the owner's complete current state, so only the intermediate transitions go unobserved. A real resync is needed only for evidence of loss (`lossCount` or `admissionRejected` changing), a reconnect, or no previous envelope.

This was found during the #74 closeout ([PR #80](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/80)). Related:
- #81, the subagent-specific case of a comet being decided by comparing against the previous snapshot;
- #90, waking on the Hub's change stream, which narrows the window but doesn't close it.

## Desired outcome

A revision gap with no loss evidence is treated as an ordinary update. A new top-level completion notice queues its comet and wave once, however many revisions the worker skipped. Running comets and existing wave epochs continue. A real loss, a reconnect or a restart keeps today's no-replay resync behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A completion arrives in a revision the worker never observes, with a later revision in the same poll. Exactly one comet is queued in Work, and the unread wave plays.
- [ ] A running comet and other tasks' wave epochs survive a revision gap.
- [ ] A `lossCount` or `admissionRejected` change, a reconnect and a first snapshot still resync without replaying old celebrations.
- [ ] A notice that was already celebrated is not celebrated again after a gap. Coordinate the "already celebrated" definition with #81.
- [ ] Stale evidence, Free/Quiet and started comet reservations keep their existing rules.

## Verification

Add focused `tests/test_shared_input.py` cases with the fake clock and isolated state that skip revisions between accepted snapshots, and run `python3 scripts/check.py`. Update the `shared-session-consumer` spec's "Restart or snapshot resync" scenario through an OpenSpec change if the resync definition changes. This is source-only work; installation and visible-device checks need separate authorization.

title: Separate shared configuration operations, runtime primitives and hook management
body:
## Desired outcome

Shared configuration behavior, runtime primitives and hook-file management have explicit owners beneath the CLI and HTTP entry points. Servers and installers import focused operations instead of receiving the bridge module or a namespace of its globals.

Start with the configuration-edit boundary: browser routes and machine commands call the same transaction-level operations without translating machine commands into browser URLs. Continue with hook management and the remaining runtime dependencies. Preserve current process and state ownership.

## Evidence

Source baseline: `97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e` (2026-09-24).

- [integration_api.operation/process](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/integration_api.py#L181-L245) translates commands into /api/... routes and imports wall_server to apply them.
- [wall_server.apply_operation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/wall_server.py#L125-L157) owns shared configuration validation/application beneath browser routing.
- [The CLI](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/bridge.py#L1534-L1541) passes a bridge namespace to shared-input and controller commands. Other server/installer callers also receive broad bridge dependencies.
- Hook-file management and its span-preserving JSON parser reside in bridge.py despite callers in shared input, installation and hook tests.
- [ADR 0008](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/docs/decisions/0008-integration-settings-extension.md#L19-L23) calls for shared transaction-level application operations and atomic configuration receipts.

## Scope and implementation sequence

1. Extract focused configuration operations independent of HTTP and the CLI. Browser routes decode browser payloads; the machine adapter validates its own contract and resolves opaque IDs. Neither the worker nor the integration application path depends on wall_server or /api/... strings.
2. Move hook management and the JSON span parser into a focused module. Preserve supported commands, bytes/positions of unrelated hooks, trust boundaries and private backups; temporary re-exports are allowed where existing callers need a staged migration.
3. Give shared runtime primitives explicit homes and dependencies: state initialization, mode changes, config/geometry loading, JSON writes, device requests and worker launch. Avoid replacing bridge.py with another catch-all runtime module.
4. Remove whole-module b/bridge arguments and the SimpleNamespace(**globals()) hand-off. Retain explicit request/send/launch/clock seams appropriate to each operation. Device reads and enrollment requests are not interchangeable with rendered-effect sends.
5. Update installation packaging for every new module. The Linux installer is the only installation path after #131.
6. Keep launch_worker spawning bridge.py worker and preserve every documented CLI command and argument.

Keep browser Host/Origin/edit-token handling and machine authentication, strict request validation, opaque IDs and request journals in their respective adapters.

Out of scope: new daemon/process ownership, schema or public API changes, rendering policy, input selection, wall-page scheduling (#119), device context (#121), transaction-duration changes, installations or device operations.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: No caller receives the bridge module or SimpleNamespace(**globals()). Imports needed only to break entry-point cycles are removed; deliberate lazy imports for optional dependencies remain allowed and documented.
- AC2: Hook management is exercised through its owning module or documented temporary re-exports. Registration/removal/rollback preserve unrelated hook text, positions, commands and trust behavior.
- AC3: Demo and affected tests inject device request/send and worker-launch dependencies through explicit seams rather than mutating the bridge module. Necessary failure injection at an owning boundary remains allowed; a blanket ban on mocking is not an objective.
- AC4: An isolated Linux runtime-copy test proves `install_linux.copy_runtime` includes every shared runtime module this change adds, and that the copied `bridge.py` imports them and starts its documented commands outside the source tree. (Refreshed 2026-09-25: #131 / PR #138 removed the Windows installer, so Linux is the only installation path.)
- AC5: The Python, browser, MCP and required workflow suites pass. CLI smoke coverage verifies documented command names/arguments and optional-dependency startup behavior; record the actual suite count at the delivery revision.
- AC6: Isolated Linux setup with fake device transport, run against the copied runtime, verifies packaging. No Windows PowerShell validation remains after #131. This evidence does not claim an installed upgrade. (Refreshed 2026-09-25.)
- AC7: A decision record using the next available number describes application-operation, runtime, hook, CLI and worker ownership and the permitted dependency direction.
- AC8: The integration/worker configuration application path imports neither wall_server nor browser route names. Both adapters invoke the same configuration operations; no duplicate edit implementation replaces the removed coupling.
- AC9: Caller-owned transactions, exactly-once revision/dirty notifications per existing edit semantics, and atomic configuration-plus-receipt commits are preserved. Cancellation, revocation, expiry and cross-client revision conflicts retain their existing outcomes.
- AC10: Browser edits retain selective active-comet deferral; machine execution retains its wait for an active comet or existing pending wall edit. Equivalent eligible edits through both adapters produce equivalent saved settings/assignments without resetting task epochs, replaying effects, changing source/mode/scene, or touching unrelated reservations.

## Verification approach

Use existing isolated SQLite, fake clocks and fake device transport. Preserve hook, source-switching, cancellation/recovery and device-isolation tests. Add focused browser/machine operation-parity checks covering deferred and conflict cases, installer packaging coverage and CLI compatibility coverage before moving the corresponding code.

Run python3 scripts/check.py, npm run test:browser, npm run test:mcp, and the workflow checks required by repository policy. Windows checks run in Windows PowerShell. Keep tests for distinct algorithms and race conditions.

This is intended to preserve behavior. Apply the SDLC's significant-design planning requirements, verify affected specs and record why no capability delta is needed if contracts remain unchanged.

## Dependencies and readiness

Strong recommendation; high confidence. Ready for source delivery. The configuration-operation extraction is the first bounded step. Coordinate the remaining broad module moves with active controller/worker owners and merge in a quiet window; do not absorb behavior fixes.

#119 is independent frontend work. #120 follows this module ownership work. #121 remains a separate device-context decision, and #122 investigates shared-input projection. #127 owns the device-render input; #128 investigates backend wall refresh/projection. #129 investigates execution ownership while preserving locks, and #130 measures contention before considering shorter lock windows.

## Delivery target

Source-only through reviewed PR delivery. This issue does not authorize installation, physical-light changes or changes to another task's worktree.

## Agreed architecture work order

1. This issue: extract shared configuration operations first, then hook management and the remaining runtime dependencies in bounded steps.
2. #119 (browser coordinator) and #127 (device-render input) are separate next candidates; neither replaces the other.
3. #120 targets backup/fixture/operation schema coupling after this issue. #128 first settles the backend refresh/freshness question.
4. #129 is a later execution-ownership investigation. #130 independently measures whether shorter lock windows are justified; no lock-duration change is implied by this refactor.

#121 and #122 keep their existing device-context and shared-projection scopes. They are related work, not additional prerequisites for the first configuration extraction. This ordering supersedes the earlier sequencing comment on this issue; issue-specific dependencies and active ownership still govern delivery.

title: Move the wall page's rebuild policy into one scheduler behind a view model
body:
## Desired outcome

The wall page decides "may the DOM rebuild now" in one place. Renderers only draw a view model; the assembly, the inspector, and the pollers stop carrying their own rebuild rules; browser checks observe the page through one small test hook instead of page globals.

Evidence at `main` 97b6b37: `bridge/wall.html` (956 lines, 41 functions) decides whether to rebuild in at least eight places: the early return in `drawWall`, `action()` ending the assembly, the poll failure path, the geometry-key check in `render()`, the hold and deferred redraw in `endAssembly`, the select guard and resync in `inspect()`, the Prism destroy-and-recreate branch, and forced `wallFingerprint=''` resets. Five fingerprints coexist (`wallFingerprint`, `projectFingerprint`, `taskFingerprint`, `detailFingerprint`, `prismGeometryKey`) plus the `taskFocus`/`selected` preservation added by #106. Every P1 and P2 the independent reviewers found in PRs #24, #35, and #40 lived here (a rejected override lingering, a human-speed click dropped by a deferred redraw, stale nodes animated during a hold), and each fix added another special case. Sixteen browser check modules reference page globals: `state` 110 times, `refresh` 126, `assembly` 43, `wallAssembly` 30, plus direct writes to `wallFingerprint`, `refreshing`, and `errorUntil`.

## Scope

- A view-model function: polled state in, drawn Lines with colors, numbers, associations, selection, pending, and rendering snapshot out; pure and unit-testable in the browser suite.
- Renderers (the standard SVG wall and Prism) that consume a prepared view model through drawing/update/destruction and assembly/finish lifecycle operations. Keep Prism, its geometry adapter and label solver as existing owners. Preserve both renderers unless #123 separately approves and delivers retirement; this issue does not remove the fallback.
- One scheduler that owns the rebuild decision given: a new poll, a selection or focus change, an interaction, an assembly in flight or held, a control with focus, and a geometry change; it preserves focus and pulse phase by contract.
- One test hook (for example `window.wallMap` with `poll(snapshot)`, `settle()`, `viewModel()`) replacing direct access to `state`, `refresh`, `wallFingerprint`, `refreshing`, `errorUntil`, and `assembly`; the sixteen check modules migrate to it.
- Behavior is pixel- and timing-identical: exact phase anchoring, focus survival across polls, 360 raw number clicks, held clicks selecting their Line, assembly completion rules, and the inspector's position retention all remain covered by the existing checks.

Out of scope: visual changes; the live renderer (#17) and the rendering snapshot contract (#15); new features.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: One coordinator owns whether and when DOM sections may rebuild, including focus and interaction holds. Rendering helpers do not independently override that policy. Local render caches may remain implementation details; completion is demonstrated by behavior and a clear ownership map, not a blanket prohibition on fingerprint variables.
- AC2: Every existing browser check passes with behavior unchanged; the migration replaces page-global access with the test hook, and no check module references `wallFingerprint`, `refreshing`, `errorUntil`, or `assembly` internals.
- AC3: The view-model function has direct checks for the associations, pending, selection, and mode cases the specs name (`wall-line-identification`, `wall-mode-presentation`, `wall-assembly-animation`, `wall-task-inspector`, `wall-current-projects`).
- AC4: The scheduler has checks for rejected override resync, human-speed and long-press clicks during assembly, Replay during a hold, geometry change and poll failure during assembly, and focused controls during a poll. Preserve the #117 regression: Open in Codex keeps keyboard focus on unchanged polls, rejected overrides resync after blur, and removed link eligibility restores focus to a surviving control. Re-read that delivery before migration.
- AC5: Screenshots at 1440, 800, and 390 px in both layouts and all three modes match the pre-change page; the user approves the UI candidate before merge per repository policy (no intended visual change, but the page is UI).
- AC6: The five wall capability specifications are verified unchanged; the PR records why no OpenSpec delta is needed.
- AC7: Both renderer paths obey the same assembly lifecycle and interruption contract. Tests observe interactions and rendered results through the public test hook; retain real DOM/pointer/keyboard coverage rather than replacing it with view-model assertions alone.

## Verification approach

TDD by moving checks first: port the existing browser modules to the test hook against the current page (green), add the view-model and scheduler checks (red), then restructure. `npm run test:browser` with `TMPDIR` on real disk; `python3 scripts/check.py` unchanged; Edge on Windows for the visual comparison. Rendering cost per frame is measured before and after using the same environment and method, with no performance gain assumed. Coordinate any actual Edge baseline with #124; Linux traces do not establish that baseline.

During test migration, absorb the scope note already recorded on this issue: use a fixture-defined hub expectation rather than reproducing the page's junction algorithm; replace fixed waits with observable conditions where practical; retain rotation/overlap and moving-target press cases. A test hook must not bypass the scheduling behavior being tested.

## Dependencies

No dependency on #118. Coordinate with #17 so the future live renderer uses the same browser coordinator. Re-read #78 and #117/PR #116 and preserve their approved behavior; those deliveries currently own overlapping UI work. Refresh their status before starting.

#123 owns the separate fallback decision. Until a removal is separately approved and delivered, design for both renderers. #124 owns actual Edge rendering-cost evidence.

title: Contain SQLite backup, fixture and operation knowledge within state owners
body:
## Desired outcome

Concentrate schema knowledge where it causes demonstrated maintenance coupling: shared-input backup/restore, synthetic demo seeding, and selected multi-table state operations. Callers express those operations without reconstructing column order or backup row formats.

The objective is a smaller change surface for schema evolution, not a wrapper for every SQL statement or a ban on all cross-module reads.

## Evidence

At `97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e`:

- [devices.py](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/devices.py#L14-L33) preserves legacy column order for positional shared-input backups.
- [shared_input._dump_tables/_restore_tables](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/shared_input.py#L253-L266) use SELECT * and interpret legacy row lengths.
- [scripts/demo.py](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/scripts/demo.py#L43-L55) seeds several tables with positional tuples; browser checks depend on that fixture.
- Shared-input projection and wall configuration edits span task, placement and project state. The useful boundary is a coherent operation, including its transaction, rather than individual SQL statements.

## Scope

- Put legacy/current backup encoding and restoration behind the modules that own the relevant state and compatibility rules. Preserve the supported backup format and restore behavior.
- Provide a state/map-owned synthetic seeding operation used by the demo and browser fixtures.
- Inventory the cross-module state operations affected by those changes and #118's configuration-operation boundary. Move a bounded operation where doing so removes column/layout or invariant knowledge from callers.
- Keep multi-table changes on the caller's transaction. Owner helpers must not open independent connections or commit behind the caller.
- Retain justified SQL projections where an owner wrapper would add no information hiding; document those choices.

Out of scope: an ORM, generic query/repository framework, schema migration, new backup format, allocation changes, moving already-owned controller/integration journals, or a repository-wide SQL rewrite.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The delivery records the bounded operations being changed, their owners, callers and invariants. Completion is measured by removed schema/row-format knowledge, not grep counts or a universal no-cross-table rule.
- AC2: The demo seeds through the owning operation. A focused Python test verifies its tasks, activity epochs, projects, metadata and applied-mode state before the browser suite uses it.
- AC3: Existing legacy and device-aware backup data restore correctly without callers inferring compatibility from tuple length. Repeated initialization and source rollback preserve current modes/scenes, manual preferences, bound placements, task epochs and each device's comet reservations.
- AC4: Failure partway through a multi-table operation rolls back as a unit; no new connection or hidden commit breaks the caller's transaction. Preserve existing source-generation checks and concurrency behavior.
- AC5: Tests for migrations, source rollback, pending edits and reservations retain their assertions. Python and browser suites pass with no behavior or wire-contract change.
- AC6: The PR explains retained cross-module SQL and why each new operation hides meaningful policy or representation. Verify affected specs and record why no capability delta is needed if requirements remain unchanged.

## Verification approach

Start with characterization of synthetic seeding and existing backup/restore behavior using isolated fixtures. Use the existing Linux pre-migration fixture, repeated-initialization, shared-input rollback, project-map and comet tests. Add only missing operation-level compatibility/atomicity coverage; do not remove distinct lower-level tests.

Run python3 scripts/check.py and npm run test:browser, plus required workflow checks for any planning/specification changes. No installed database or physical device is needed.

## Dependencies and readiness

- #118 first: use the settled application/runtime ownership rather than moving SQL twice.
- #127 and #128 address render inputs and wall refresh/projection separately; this issue changes neither rendering policy nor refresh scheduling.
- Coordinate any change to shared-input projection with #122 and active source-input fixes; this issue does not depend on extracting a pure shared reducer.
- Worth exploring, with high confidence in the observed coupling and moderate confidence in broad payoff. Keep the initial scope on backups and seeding, expanding only when a named caller demonstrably loses schema knowledge.

Backlog and blocked by #118. Once that source change lands, re-read the callers and select the bounded operation set before implementation.

## Delivery target

Source-only. No schema change, installation, runtime database migration or device operation.

title: Carry device identity as a worker context instead of threading parameters
body:
## Desired outcome

The worker carries one device context instead of threading a `device` parameter through every function and branching on "is this the primary device" at each step. Adding a third device kind, or moving a responsibility between devices, then touches one place.

Evidence at `main` 97b6b37: #67 introduced per-device workers by adding `device=devices.DEFAULT` to eleven function signatures and 41 call sites in `bridge/bridge.py`, plus `devices.meta_key(name, device)` lookups in five modules. `run_worker` (218 lines) branches on `primary` eleven times to decide which device polls the shared feed, owns the controller journal, applies overrides, and reconciles read state. Two recorded pitfalls come from this shape: tests that patch `run_worker` for `main()` must accept `device` and `feed` keyword arguments or the retry loop spins, and a worker in Quiet never exits without a scheduled mode change.

## Scope

- A device context value (identity, meta-key prefix, lock and scene file names, config, primary flag, feed poller) created once per worker pass and passed to the functions that need it.
- Primary-only responsibilities (shared feed polling, controller journal and controls, overrides, read reconciliation) provided by the Lines device's context rather than inline `if primary` branches, so a non-primary device carries no-op implementations.
- Behavior is unchanged: one light writer per device, the same lock files, the same meta keys, the same feed ownership, the same recovery on failure.

Out of scope: new device kinds; combining devices into one layout (#47); wall-map device switching (#44); any change to the controller contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `bridge.py` functions no longer carry a `device=` default parameter for state lookups; the context supplies it (a signature list in the PR evidence).
- AC2: `run_worker` contains no `if primary` branches; the primary-only behavior is exercised by the existing per-device worker tests and by a test that runs a non-primary device with the no-op context.
- AC3: Every existing Python test passes, including `tests/test_device_worker.py`, `tests/test_controller_worker.py`, `tests/test_shared_input.py`, and the enrollment and panels suites; the lock file names and meta keys read from an installed database are byte-identical before and after (fixture comparison in `tests/fixtures/linux-state-v4`).
- AC4: The `main()` retry loop and its test double accept the context without keyword-argument coupling; the recorded pitfall about `device`/`feed` kwargs no longer applies.
- AC5: The `device-worker` and `device-state` specifications are verified unchanged; the PR records why no OpenSpec delta is needed. If the design settles the ownership of primary responsibilities differently from ADR 0010, a decision record amendment is required.

## Verification approach

Fake-clock worker suites first; a new non-primary context test written red. Full Python suite, browser suite, MCP checks. Expect several independent review rounds, as every worker change in this repository has needed; give each round the prior findings. Windows PowerShell checks are local.

## Dependencies

- #118 first (the worker and primitives split).
- Blocked while worker changes from #111, #112, and #115 are in flight; start after they merge to avoid rebasing a structural change across behavior fixes.

title: Investigate a pure shared-input projection function
body:
## Desired outcome

Determine whether the shared-input projection can be a pure function from (previous envelope, new envelope, prior rows) to a row diff, tested without SQLite, so arrival-order and freshness rules can be exercised exhaustively.

title: Decide whether the standard wall renderer remains a fallback for Prism
body:
## Desired outcome

One decision on the wall page's renderer set: keep the standard SVG wall as a fallback when the Prism assets or connector layout are unavailable, or retire it and treat a missing Prism asset as an installation error.

At `main` 97b6b37 the page keeps both: `drawStandardWall()` with its own assembly, and the Prism renderer with its own (`bridge/wall.html` 529-692, `bridge/prism.js`). Both are covered by the browser suite (sixteen modules), so every wall change is verified twice, and the two assemblies have already drifted (hub-seeded unfolding and connector flares in the standard path; `ASSEMBLY_SECONDS` and crystal materials in Prism).

## Scope

A decision, recorded on this issue and, if it has lasting consequences, in a decision record. title: Separate device render inputs from runtime configuration and transport
body:
## Desired outcome

Build one explicit device-render input for each worker pass. Rendering and display-cache decisions consume that input; credentials, file paths, clocks used for transport receipts, and transport callbacks remain with their runtime owners.

This is a maintainability change. The assessment found shared mutable input and manually maintained cache dependencies, not a demonstrated credential leak or rendering failure.

## Evidence

Source baseline: `97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e` (2026-09-24).

- [Project presentation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/project_map.py#L221-L230) adds style, coverage and signatures to `config`.
- [Shared-input suppression](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/shared_input.py#L554-L559) adds steady slots, suppressed waves and a cutoff.
- [The worker](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/bridge.py#L954-L983) assembles Locate, comet and task state in the same dictionary used by the sender.
- [Display caching](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/bridge.py#L748-L765) separately enumerates rendering dependencies; [effect_payload/render](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/bridge.py#L338-L387) provide an existing pure-computation/transport boundary.

## Scope

- Identify the complete input to effect generation, brightness policy, output receipts and cache invalidation; distinguish stable device geometry, per-pass presentation and sender-only dependencies.
- Construct a fresh render input from one coherent worker pass. Do not expose mutable aliases that let a later pass change an earlier input.
- Keep pure effect generation separate from transport and credential lookup. Preserve device identity on receipts and the existing sender test seam.
- Make the cache identity explicit alongside the render input. Preserve deliberate invalidation by modes, overrides, scene ownership and effect transitions; do not invalidate every poll merely because the sampling time changed.
- Preserve the current schemas, public APIs and rendered output.

Out of scope: the browser scheduler (#119), new effects or palettes, changing input authority, device context redesign (#121), shorter SQLite transactions, or installing the runtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The proposed input fields and their producers/consumers are documented in the change design. Pure rendering needs no credential or transport callback; no rendering policy reads hidden mutable runtime fields.
- AC2: Deterministic Lines and NL22 fixtures produce the same effect payload, brightness decisions and receipt data as the pre-change path, apart from controlled clock values.
- AC3: Tests cover pulse epochs, blocked/question precedence, Quiet/Free, project halves and coverage, stale/steady suppression, Locate, active comet sources and Lines/Panels differences. Existing algorithm tests remain.
- AC4: Cache checks cover each output-affecting setting and intentional invalidation path, including native brightness overrides. Unchanged polling does not resend or replay completed effects; a color edit updates output without restarting a task pulse or comet.
- AC5: Building a later render input cannot mutate a previously prepared input. Transport failure still leaves the previous successful rendering receipt intact and reports uncertainty through the existing path.
- AC6: The Python suite and relevant browser/API and MCP checks pass. Existing rendering-snapshot, device-worker and Panels contracts are verified; record why no capability delta is required if behavior remains unchanged.

## Verification approach

Use existing fake clocks, synthetic geometry and fake transport. Retain `tests/test_bridge.py`, `test_comets.py`, `test_modes.py`, `test_panels.py`, `test_device_worker.py`, rendering-receipt checks, and `test_project_map.py::test_color_edit_invalidates_display_without_pulse_or_comet_replay`. Add only the input-isolation and cache-dependency coverage needed for this boundary.

Run `python3 scripts/check.py`; run browser/API, MCP and workflow checks as required by the affected files and repository policy. Source equivalence does not establish installed or physical parity.

## Dependencies and readiness

Worth exploring; high confidence in the coupling, medium migration cost. Backlog until the input/cache boundary and caller migration are reviewed. Coordinate ownership and merge order with #118, #121 and overlapping worker/shared-input fixes, especially #115. These are source-overlap constraints, not a requirement to implement device contexts first.

The browser view model in #119 and reusable live renderer in #17 have different purposes; this work does not merge their contracts with the device-render input.

## Delivery target

Source-only, through a separately started implementation task and reviewed PR. No installation, live metadata access or physical-light operations.

title: Investigate separating wall-state projection from refresh work
body:
## Desired outcome

Decide whether wall-state construction can become a pure read projection while metadata refresh and drawing-cache maintenance remain explicit operations with clear owners. Establish how metadata stays fresh when a legacy worker has exited before proposing an implementation.

## Evidence

At `97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e`, [App.state](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/wall_server.py#L41-L100) combines connector-cache retries, possible device geometry reads, metadata synchronization, database mutation, presentation construction and worker launch. The [worker repeats legacy metadata refresh/synchronization](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/bridge.py#L870-L900), but [can exit when idle](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/bridge.py#L1033-L1040). [App.rendering](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/wall_server.py#L102-L111) already provides a pure-read example.

The diagnosis is structural; no measured endpoint performance regression is claimed.

## Scope and stop condition

A bounded investigation, with findings on this issue. Trace GET /api/state, legacy metadata enrichment, shared metadata enrichment, connector-cache maintenance and worker wake/exit behavior.

Identify what can be centralized without making local metadata authoritative for session lifecycle. Compare a pure projector with unchanged refresh scheduling against a separately scheduled refresh owner. Keep an explicit no-change option.

Stop with a recommended boundary, its idle/freshness contract, affected callers and tests, and either a bounded implementation scope or reasons to retain the current design. No source, test, specification or runtime changes are included.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Map every side effect in App.state and its current owner at a stated revision: state initialization, metadata writes, dirty marking, geometry acquisition/cache writes and worker launch.
- AC2: Specify expected behavior when the map remains open while a legacy worker is idle, metadata changes, input switches, or metadata becomes unavailable. Explain how titles, project assignments and Desktop-link eligibility stay current without resurrecting retired shared sessions.
- AC3: Keep connector drawing-cache ownership with the map. Preserve bounded retries, complete old/new reads, cache invalidation, fallback, and protection of shared layout.json. Address the wall-connector-geometry specification explicitly.
- AC4: Keep the wall's private presentation separate from sanitized controller/integration projections and output receipts. Pure reads must not allocate elements, clear notices, advance effects or become another light writer.

- AC6: Record costs, unresolved decisions and proceed/no-change disposition. If useful, draft a separately scoped implementation issue; completing this investigation does not require implementation.

## Verification approach

Read source, specifications and existing tests. Any illustrative experiment must use synthetic state and fake transport, with no installed state or device access. Preserve existing tests that cover distinct integration behavior rather than replacing them all with projector tests.

Lower-priority investigation after the first configuration-boundary work. No functional prerequisite for investigation. Coordinate any later implementation with #118 and #120.

Distinct from #119 (browser DOM scheduling) and #122 (shared-feed lifecycle projection). Related presentation changes such as #78 and #117 must be re-read before implementation; this issue does not take over their active deliveries.

title: Investigate one owner for worker execution transactions and journaling
body:
## Desired outcome

Determine whether the worker apply cycle can have one explicit owner for transaction boundaries, validity checks and transmission journaling, preserving the current lock windows and observable behavior.

This concerns maintainability. It does not authorize moving device sends outside SQLite transactions or claim a latency improvement.

## Evidence

At `97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e`, [run_worker](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/bridge.py#L954-L1032) prepares state, opens the apply transaction and checks revisions. [Execution.call](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/bridge/controller_state.py#L198-L225) commits and reopens that caller-owned connection while journaling transport. The outer loop must account for those intervening commits before clearing dirty state or exiting.

[ADR 0010](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/97b6b37fcbf93061adda9afab253517cee24996e/docs/decisions/0010-per-device-worker-and-nl22.md) deliberately retains one worker per device and shared-state lock windows.

## Scope and stop condition

Bounded source investigation: map the apply cycle's commits, lock ownership, guards, journal transitions and effect boundaries. Compare concentrating the existing protocol behind an execution owner with retaining the present structure.

Keep observation, rendering preparation, scheduling and device-context concerns distinguishable. A wrapper that leaves callers coordinating the same hidden commits is not sufficient.

Stop with an execution-boundary sketch and verification plan, or a supported no-change conclusion. No implementation, schema/API change, lock-duration change, live state access or device operation.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Trace normal mode application, native controls, previews, scene restoration, failure and restart. Identify who owns each transaction and which callee can commit it.
- AC2: State the caller knowledge that would disappear and where it would move. Compare migration cost against that reduction; do not rank by file size or number of branches.
- AC3: Preserve one writer per device; wall-only ownership of shared polling, controller/integration requests and holds; idempotent shared read/metadata reconciliation by every device; mode/control ordering, Free handoff, reservations and epochs.
- AC4: Preserve journal-before-send, completed/uncertain operation evidence, cancellation/revocation/generation rechecks, crash recovery, holds and no automatic replay of uncertain requests.
- AC5: Map existing race tests to each boundary, including generation/revocation between operations, controls admitted between journaled sends, partial transmission, expiry and restart. Identify missing coverage without replacing distinct low-level tests.
- AC6: Recommend a bounded behavior-preserving implementation or no change. Any proposal to shorten lock windows is recorded as a separate concurrency decision and excluded from the implementation scope.

## Verification approach

Inspect `tests/test_controller_worker.py`, `test_controller_state.py`, `test_controller_controls.py`, `test_device_worker.py` and `test_scene_restore.py`. Use fake clocks, isolated SQLite and fake transport if an experiment is needed. Report actual checks and limits; do not infer physical outcomes from receipts.

A later implementation requires the repository's significant-design plan and exact preservation checks; update decision records only if lasting ownership choices change.

## Dependencies and readiness

Later investigation, after the higher-priority module and render boundaries are understood. No functional prerequisite for source analysis; refresh #118, #121, #111, #112 and #115 before recommending a delivery sequence. Existing owners retain their work.

Device identity/context (#121), shared-feed projection (#122), and the device-render input (#127) are adjacent boundaries, not substitutes for transaction ownership.

## Delivery target

Findings and proceed/no-change disposition on this issue. Any implementation is a separate, scoped follow-up.
